Focusing on incompressible isotropic hyperelasticity, FE-MAD is evaluated on three open experimental datasets: (1) full digital image correlation (DIC) of a perforated tensile specimen, (2) a reduced-data scenario with a one-dimensional stretch profile and global force-displacement curve, and (3) a heterogeneous matrix-inclusion system in which both phases constitutive laws are identified and generalized to twenty-two previously unseen samples.
tldr: This paper presents a finite element-based framework for learning constitutive neural network models from full-field deformation data using automatic differentiation.
motivation: Traditional calibration methods for material models rely on homogeneous stress-strain experiments, which are often impractical; existing approaches for heterogeneous data suffer from computational cost, noise sensitivity, or data requirements.
method: The authors integrate a constitutive neural network within a JAX-FEM nonlinear solver and use automatic differentiation to compute gradients for parameter identification via measurement-mismatch minimization.
result: The framework is demonstrated on three experimental datasets for incompressible isotropic hyperelasticity, showing successful identification of constitutive parameters and generalization to unseen samples.
conclusion: FE-MAD provides an efficient and robust alternative for material model identification, with potential extensions to other constitutive laws and experimental setups.

title: A Differentiable Machine Learning Small-angle X-ray Scattering Analysis Framework For Structure Elucidation Of Lipid Nanoparticles
authors: Maria B{\aa}nkestad, Sandra Barman, Magnus R\"oding, Erik Kaunisto, Viktoriia Meklesh, Audrey Gallud, Marco Mendez, Marianna Yanez Arteta, Stefan Norberg, Ann Terry, Smita Chakraborty, Shun Yu, Jerk R\"onnols, Sepideh Pashami
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05200v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) are efficient delivery systems for negatively charged nucleic acids. Their multi-component architecture yields a core-shell structure. Small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS) is an important characterization technique for LNPs, but recovering internal structure and size distribution from SAXS is an inverse problem with non-unique solutions. Realistic models are often too expensive for systematic exploration. We introduce a machine-learning-accelerated, differentiable framework for SAXS analysis of heterogeneous, polydisperse LNPs. The forward model combines a core-shell particle with a Gaussian random-field interior, a neural surrogate for the monodisperse SAXS map, and a differentiable layer integrating over particle-size distributions. The surrogate reduces prediction cost by four orders of magnitude, while differentiability enables large-scale multi-start fitting and ensemble identifiability analysis. Applied to synthetic and experimental MC3 LNP data, the framework shows that near-identical SAXS fits can arise from distinct parameter modes, with the experimental fits dominated by a trade-off between size-distribution and interior-structure parameters.
tldr: A machine-learning-accelerated SAXS analysis framework for lipid nanoparticles is introduced, using a neural surrogate and differentiable programming to efficiently explore parameter space and identify degeneracies.
motivation: SAXS analysis of lipid nanoparticles is an ill-posed inverse problem; realistic models are computationally expensive, hindering systematic exploration.
method: The framework combines a core-shell particle model with a Gaussian random-field interior, a neural surrogate for the monodisperse SAXS map, and a differentiable layer for polydisperse size distributions, enabling gradient-based optimization.
result: The surrogate reduces prediction cost by four orders of magnitude; multi-start fitting reveals that near-identical SAXS fits can arise from distinct parameter modes, with trade-offs between size-distribution and interior-structure parameters.
conclusion: The framework enables efficient identifiability analysis and could be extended to other nanoparticle systems, but the paper focuses on materials science rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Multi-Fidelity Learning With Shallow Recurrent Decoders For Reactor Physics
authors: Stefano Riva, Carolina Introini, J. Nathan Kutz, Antonio Cammi
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05202v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In reactor physics, neutronics can be treated with different fidelity levels, according to the needs of the user. On one hand, the precise modeling of neutrons' behaviour in reactor physics is often expensive and time-consuming due to the high computational costs to numerically solve the Boltzmann transport equation. Conversely, by adopting suitable assumptions, such as the SP[MATH], diffusion theory, and point kinetics, it is possible to generate efficiently low-fidelity data. From the perspective of surrogate models, this computational limitation translates into a scarcity of high-fidelity data and a significant amount of low-fidelity data. Given this difference in fidelity levels, it would be interesting to develop a suitable procedure to map low-fidelity models towards higher fidelity models; for instance, one could obtain the solution to a multi-group diffusion equation starting from time-series data obtained from a point kinetics model. Indeed, this work investigates this possibility by leveraging multi-fidelity information with Shallow Recurrent Decoders, a novel machine learning architecture able to map time-series observations to the full state of the reactor. This technique has been designed to use local or global measurements as input and map their temporal trajectories to the high-dimensional state; by the same logic, in principle, this architecture can also be used when the input is formed by the solution of a lumped model. This work applies this idea to a benchmark reactor geometry, mapping the point kinetics model to the diffusion solution under various input conditions, with much less computational costs.
tldr: This paper uses multi-fidelity learning with shallow recurrent decoders to map low-fidelity point kinetics models to high-fidelity diffusion solutions in reactor physics.
motivation: High-fidelity neutronics simulations are computationally expensive, while low-fidelity models are cheap but inaccurate. The authors aim to develop a surrogate model that leverages abundant low-fidelity data to predict high-fidelity states efficiently.
method: They employ Shallow Recurrent Decoders, a machine learning architecture that maps time-series observations (from low-fidelity models) to the full high-dimensional reactor state, trained on multi-fidelity data.
result: The method successfully maps point kinetics model outputs to diffusion solutions for a benchmark reactor geometry under various input conditions, achieving much lower computational cost than direct high-fidelity simulation.
conclusion: The approach demonstrates a practical way to combine low- and high-fidelity data for reactor physics, but its applicability to other domains or more complex geometries remains to be explored.

title: Time-frequency Analysis Of Nonlinear Compton Scattering Via Joint Probability Distributions
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05203v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The interaction of charged particles with an intense laser pulse gives rise to a number of characteristic spectral features of emitted radiation, including the generation of harmonics, spectral broadening due to the phase-dependent ponderomotive red shift, and the emergence of intricate sub-harmonic structures. These effects are accumulated over the course of the interaction with the electromagnetic field and are therefore inherently nonlocal in nature. For a deeper understanding of strong-field quantum electrodynamics (SFQED) processes and their practical applications, it is desirable to employ tools that enable simultaneous analysis in the time and energy domains. In time-frequency analysis, such tools are provided by joint distributions (JDs). In this work, we demonstrate how a JD can be devised within the SFQED framework. Specifically, we focus on constructing a non-negative JD, which allows for a clear probabilistic interpretation. We study the properties of the proposed distribution and test its utility by applying it to the nonlinear Compton scattering in complex laser pulse configurations with carrier-envelope phase and variable polarization.
tldr: This paper develops a non-negative joint probability distribution for time-frequency analysis of nonlinear Compton scattering in strong-field QED.
motivation: To understand spectral features like harmonics and ponderomotive red shift that are nonlocal in time, requiring simultaneous time-energy analysis.
method: Constructs a non-negative joint distribution within the SFQED framework, applied to nonlinear Compton scattering with complex laser pulses.
result: Demonstrates the utility of the joint distribution for analyzing carrier-envelope phase and polarization effects.
conclusion: Provides a new tool for time-frequency analysis in SFQED, but no direct connection to the user's research interests.

title: Spatial Resolution Of X-ray Beam-tracking Microscopy
authors: Harry Allan, Carlos Navarrete-Le\'on, Adam Doherty, Shashidhara Marathe, Kaz Wanelik, Marco Endrizzi
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05269v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: X-ray beam-tracking is a phase-contrast imaging technique capable of simultaneously retrieving transmission, phase, and dark-field images. Although the spatial resolution in beam-tracking is largely considered to be 'aperture driven', no model yet exists to describe this in full. The dark-field channel is of particular interest, due to previous observations of anomalously high sharpness compared to transmission and phase channels. We derive a full optical transfer function model for each contrast channel using the Fokker-Planck equation for near-field imaging. Experimental validation using both synchrotron-based and laboratory-based setups, with 15 um circular and 10 um rectangular apertures, reveals a limiting resolution of at least 3 um, much smaller than the apertures themselves. Together, the model and the supporting experiments offer a full description of spatial resolution in beam-tracking, and formally confirm the greater spatial resolution in the dark-field channel. These findings open new possibilities in system design and experimental protocols to exploit these capabilities.
tldr: This paper develops an optical transfer function model for X-ray beam-tracking microscopy, demonstrating that spatial resolution in the dark-field channel can exceed the aperture size.
motivation: To understand and quantify the spatial resolution in X-ray beam-tracking phase-contrast imaging, especially the anomalously high sharpness observed in the dark-field channel.
method: Derived a full optical transfer function model using the Fokker-Planck equation for near-field imaging, and validated experimentally with synchrotron and laboratory setups using circular and rectangular apertures.
result: The model predicts and experiments confirm a limiting resolution of at least 3 µm, much smaller than the 10-15 µm apertures, with the dark-field channel showing higher resolution than transmission and phase channels.
conclusion: The findings provide a complete description of spatial resolution in beam-tracking, enabling new system designs and experimental protocols to exploit the enhanced dark-field resolution.

title: Opinion Dynamics On Social Proximity Disordered Networks
authors: Fellipe Aranha, Giuliano G. Porci\'uncula, Adauto J. F. de Souza, Paulo R. A. Campos, Andr\'e L. M. Vilela
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05349v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Understanding how local social pressure shapes collective opinion formation is essential in modern society, with implications in sociology, politics, finance, and technology. Complex networks are a powerful framework for investigating these processes and for representing social interactions in emergent phenomena, and canonical models such as random, scale-free, and small-world networks remain most relevant when Euclidean geometric proximity and contiguous interactions are not the dominant organizing factors. Our investigation explores the effects of Gabriel graphs, a spatially embedded network that utilizes proximity-based interactions, on social opinion dynamics. Using a geometric disorder parameter that randomly displaces agent coordinates, we transition from square lattices of social interactions to spatial random networks that preserve local constraints while introducing strong topological heterogeneity. Opinion dynamics operate through social pressure, with a level of nonconformity that affects dissent among opinions. We analyze magnetization, susceptibility, and Binder's fourth-order cumulant to characterize the emergence and breakdown of global social consensus. The model exhibits second-order phase transitions whose behavior depends on both geometric disorder and nonconformity levels. We use volumetric scaling and provide a reference frame appropriate for characterizing criticality in regular and heterogeneous interaction topologies. We find that the standard critical exponents remain compatible with the two-dimensional Ising universality class. Furthermore, the results suggest that spatially constrained, planar, and globally connected interaction topologies preserve the dimensionality of space in critical dynamics analysis.
tldr: This paper studies opinion dynamics on spatially embedded networks with geometric disorder, finding second-order phase transitions in the 2D Ising universality class.
motivation: To understand how local social pressure and geometric disorder affect collective opinion formation in spatially constrained networks.
method: Simulations of opinion dynamics on Gabriel graphs with varying geometric disorder, using magnetization, susceptibility, and Binder cumulant to analyze phase transitions.
result: The model exhibits second-order phase transitions with critical exponents consistent with the 2D Ising universality class, and geometric disorder does not change the universality class.
conclusion: Spatially constrained planar networks preserve the dimensionality of space in critical dynamics, suggesting robustness of Ising criticality in such topologies.

title: A Stochastic Model For Fog Forecasting
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05590v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Despite significant advancements in parameterizations of boundary layer processes, forecasting, and nowcasting low-level clouds using numerical models remain challenging. The purpose of this study is to test a prototype of a high-resolution stochastic-deterministic model designed to simulate the life cycle of fog cover based on the Ising model from statistical mechanics. The case of advection fog around St. John's Airport in Newfoundland (Canada) has been considered. The model demonstrates promising capabilities in forecasting mean fog cover and replicating the horizontal structure observed in satellite imagery, including bands, rolls, and closed or open cells. We evaluate the model's predictive skill by analyzing its effectiveness in reproducing the evolution of fog cover across three representative cases. A contingency table and associated performance metrics are used to assess its accuracy.
tldr: This paper uses an Ising model from statistical mechanics to simulate fog cover, but it is unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Fog forecasting is challenging for numerical models; the authors aim to test a stochastic-deterministic model based on the Ising model to improve fog cover prediction.
method: A high-resolution stochastic-deterministic model based on the Ising model is developed and applied to advection fog cases around St. John's Airport, Newfoundland. The model's predictive skill is evaluated using contingency tables and performance metrics.
result: The model shows promising capabilities in forecasting mean fog cover and replicating horizontal structures (bands, rolls, cells) observed in satellite imagery.
conclusion: The Ising-based model offers a new approach for fog forecasting, but further validation and refinement are needed.

title: Stereotyping By Strategy Standing Diversifies Cooperation Patterns In Indirect Reciprocity
authors: Ming Wei, Xin Wang, Wenqiang Zhu, Longzhao Liu, Hongwei Zheng, Feng Fu, Shaoting Tang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05591v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Indirect reciprocity explains how cooperation evolves through social reputations. People observe others, assign reputations, and condition their future actions on these assignments. This process is cognitively demanding, and stereotyping offers a simpler alternative by replacing individual-level reputation with group-level information. Theoretical models commonly implement stereotyping through exogenously given group labels. In real societies, however, group-level impressions may be associated with observable patterns of behavior. Here we propose a framework of stereotyping by strategy standing, in which mutants may condition their actions on the overall reputation level associated with a resident strategy rather than on the recipient's reputation. We show that this form of stereotyping can diversify stable cooperation in indirect reciprocity. As the strength of stereotyping increases, additional cooperative evolutionarily stable norm-strategy (ESS) pairs emerge in substantial numbers. In particular, we identify eight highly cooperative ESS pairs that become stable under very weak stereotyping. These pairs, which we call the counterparts of the leading eight, share the same social norms as the classical leading eight and differ only in how they prescribe behavior between bad individuals. They are unstable without stereotyping because they can be invaded by their corresponding leading strategies, but they become stable once stereotyping exceeds a critical threshold. Our results suggest that group-level impressions based on strategy standing can provide a coarse-grained informational route to stable cooperation and offer a more behaviorally grounded perspective on how stereotyping affects indirect reciprocity.
tldr: This paper studies how stereotyping based on strategy standing can stabilize cooperation in indirect reciprocity, but it is unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand how group-level impressions (stereotyping) can promote cooperation in social dilemmas, moving beyond individual reputations.
method: Evolutionary game theory with a model where mutants condition actions on the overall reputation of a resident strategy; analysis of evolutionary stable strategies (ESS) under varying stereotyping strength.
result: Stereotyping by strategy standing yields additional cooperative ESS pairs, including eight counterparts of the leading eight norms that become stable above a critical stereotyping threshold.
conclusion: Group-level impressions based on strategy standing offer a behaviorally grounded route to stable cooperation, but the work is purely in social evolution and not relevant to the user's research interests.

title: Passively Synchronized Dual-color Mode-locked Fiber Lasers Based On Nonlinear Amplifying Loop Mirrors
authors: Jing Zeng, Bowen Li, Qiang Hao, Ming Yan, Kun Huang, Heping Zeng
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05595v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We have proposed and implemented a novel scheme for passive all-optical synchronization between erbium and ytterbium mode-locked fiber lasers. The passive locking of repetition rates for the dual-color pulses was realized by cross-phase modulation within phase-biased nonlinear amplifying loop mirrors. In contrast to previous demonstrations, the synchronization system was configured in an all-polarization-maintaining structure, thus gaining substantially improved stability and robustness. Consequently, the maximum tolerance of cavity-length mismatch of 16.2 mm was achieved unprecedentedly, which was at least one order of magnitude longer than previously reported results for comparable temporal durations of involved pulses. The corresponding relative timing jitter was measured to be 31 fs within 1-MHz bandwidth. Such tight and robust synchronization fiber laser system offers a great potential for various applications, such as pump-probe microscopy, Raman scattering spectroscopy and nonlinear frequency generation.
tldr: This paper presents a passively synchronized dual-color mode-locked fiber laser system using nonlinear amplifying loop mirrors, achieving robust synchronization with low jitter.
motivation: To improve the stability and robustness of dual-color pulse synchronization for applications like pump-probe microscopy and nonlinear frequency generation.
method: The authors use cross-phase modulation within phase-biased nonlinear amplifying loop mirrors in an all-polarization-maintaining fiber structure to passively lock repetition rates of erbium and ytterbium fiber lasers.
result: Achieved a cavity-length mismatch tolerance of 16.2 mm (order of magnitude improvement) and relative timing jitter of 31 fs within 1-MHz bandwidth.
conclusion: The demonstrated synchronization system offers robust performance suitable for practical applications in ultrafast optics and spectroscopy.

title: Controlled Generation Of Ultrafast Vector Vortex Beams From A Mode-locked Fiber Laser
authors: Kun Huang, Jing Zeng, Jiwei Gan, Qiang Hao, Heping Zeng
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05612v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We report on a new class of mode-locked fiber laser that allows direct creation of ultrafast vector vortex beams at arbitrary positions on the higher-order Poincar\'{e} sphere. The on-demand generation of space-variant polarization patterns was realized by controlling geometric phases inside the laser resonator to map polarization to orbital angular momentum. Thanks to the ingenious cavity design, the required intracavity manipulation of the geometric phase imposed no disturbance on the passively mode-locked operation, thus demonstrating robust and flexible switching of vectorial modes with a 8.5-ps pulse duration. Analytical expressions were deduced to model the generated cylindrically-symmetric polarization profiles, and agreed exceedingly well with experimental observations. The presented fiber laser would constitute a compact light source for producing ultrafast pulses in high-purity structured modes, which may find broad applications in classical and quantum optics.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a mode-locked fiber laser that generates ultrafast vector vortex beams with controlled polarization patterns.
motivation: To create a compact source of ultrafast structured light beams with arbitrary space-variant polarization for applications in classical and quantum optics.
method: Geometric phases are controlled inside the laser resonator to map polarization to orbital angular momentum, enabling on-demand generation of vector vortex beams without disturbing mode-locking.
result: Robust and flexible switching of vectorial modes with 8.5-ps pulse duration was achieved, and analytical models matched experimental observations.
conclusion: The fiber laser provides a compact source for high-purity structured ultrafast pulses, with potential applications in classical and quantum optics.

title: Aberration-Free Optical Spectrometer
authors: Qingze Guan, Zi Heng Lim, Xinchen Wan, Yixiu Shen, Guangya Zhou
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05686v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Optical spectrometers are fundamental to scientific analysis, yet achieving high performance at low cost remains challenging because uncorrected aberrations rapidly degrade spectral resolution and typically necessitate complex, expensive optics. Moreover, to preserve spectral resolution, many compact designs remain fundamentally throughput-limited in terms of having a high f-number and a narrow slit. Here we present SHADES (Stochastic High-throughput Aberration-free Deep-Encoded Spectrometer), a general framework that mitigates the effects of optical aberrations using a stochastic grating array (SGA) coupled with physically grounded deep learning (DL), while substantially increasing optical throughput using encoded multi-slits. We develop a theoretical framework establishing aberration resilient spectroscopy in compact, highly aberrated systems, enabling miniaturization without sacrificing spectral resolution and optical throughput. SHADES utilizes an arbitrary spectrum generator (ASG) for hardware-in-the-loop calibration with a DL-based reconstruction pipeline. We further leverage transfer learning (TL) to reduce calibration data and computation for scalable deployment of SHADES. Experimentally, a micro-SHADES prototype achieves a spectral resolution of 2.4 nm over 450-700 nm and accurately reconstructs fluorescence spectra for chemical identification. Collectively, SHADES provides an aberration-free, high-throughput, low-cost spectrometer architecture suited for compact and scalable sensing applications.
tldr: SHADES uses a stochastic grating array and deep learning to achieve aberration-free, high-throughput optical spectrometry in compact systems.
motivation: Conventional spectrometers suffer from aberrations that degrade resolution and require expensive optics; compact designs are throughput-limited.
method: A stochastic grating array (SGA) is coupled with physically grounded deep learning (DL) for reconstruction, and an arbitrary spectrum generator (ASG) enables hardware-in-the-loop calibration; transfer learning reduces calibration data.
result: A micro-SHADES prototype achieves 2.4 nm spectral resolution over 450-700 nm and accurately reconstructs fluorescence spectra.
conclusion: SHADES provides a low-cost, compact, high-throughput spectrometer architecture suitable for scalable sensing applications.

title: Optical Chirality Of Membrane Metasurfaces With Broken In-plane Symmetry
authors: Ivan Toftul, Brijesh Kumar, Maxim Gorkunov, Yuri Kivshar
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05775v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study chiroptical properties of single-layer dielectric membrane metasurfaces with broken in-plane symmetry. In sharp contrast to a common belief that chiral optical phenomena require symmetry breaking in the vertical direction, we show that flat single-layer metasurfaces are capable of strong specific chiral effects. Although the single-layer geometry forbids conventional co-polarized circular dichroism, strong resonant conversion circular dichroism appears to be possible in particular wavelength ranges determined by the spectra of photonic eigenmodes. We explore its origin starting with a [MATH] rotation-symmetric and in-plane mirror-symmetric membrane metasurface and applying to it various in-plane perturbations. Simultaneously breaking of the in-plane mirror symmetry and lifting the rotation symmetry unlocks resonantly enhanced circular conversion dichroism. We derive selection rules for this effect and trace its origin to eigenmode interference and intercoupling using chiral coupled-mode theory.
tldr: This paper studies chiroptical effects in single-layer dielectric membrane metasurfaces with broken in-plane symmetry, showing that strong circular conversion dichroism can occur without vertical symmetry breaking.
motivation: To challenge the common belief that chiral optical phenomena require vertical symmetry breaking, and to explore the potential of flat single-layer metasurfaces for chiroptical applications.
method: The authors start with a rotation-symmetric and in-plane mirror-symmetric membrane metasurface, then apply in-plane perturbations to break symmetries. They use chiral coupled-mode theory to derive selection rules and trace the origin of circular conversion dichroism to eigenmode interference and intercoupling.
result: Strong resonant conversion circular dichroism is possible in single-layer metasurfaces when both in-plane mirror symmetry and rotation symmetry are broken, despite the absence of conventional co-polarized circular dichroism.
conclusion: The findings open new possibilities for flat, single-layer chiral photonic devices, with implications for sensing, imaging, and polarization control.

title: On Leadership Emergence In Opinion Dynamics On Social Networks
authors: Martina Alutto, Lorenzo Zino, Karl H. Johansson, Angela Fontan
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05825v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Leadership in social groups emerges dynamically through interaction and opinion exchange. Empirical evidence indicates that individuals expressing strong opinions tend to gain influence, while sustained leadership critically depends on maintaining alignment with the surrounding social context. Motivated by these observations, we introduce a coupled dynamical model describing the simultaneous evolution of opinions and leadership in a networked population. Extending the Friedkin-Johnsen framework, we represent leadership as a time-varying susceptibility to social influence, which evolves according to a game-theoretic mechanism, consistent with social psychology evidence. Within this setting, agents strengthen their leadership by expressing decisive yet socially coherent opinions, whereas misalignment with the collective state results in a loss of influence. We analyze the coupled dynamics and establish sufficient conditions to identify which agents necessarily emerge as leaders and which act as followers in the social network.
tldr: This paper models leadership emergence in social networks using a coupled opinion-leadership dynamics framework, but does not address quantum or thermodynamic aspects.
motivation: To understand how leadership emerges dynamically in social groups through opinion exchange, based on empirical evidence that strong opinions and social alignment influence leadership.
method: Extends the Friedkin-Johnsen opinion dynamics model by introducing a time-varying susceptibility to social influence that evolves via a game-theoretic mechanism, coupling opinion and leadership dynamics.
result: Establishes sufficient conditions to identify which agents necessarily become leaders and which become followers in a social network.
conclusion: The model provides insights into leadership emergence in social networks, with potential applications in understanding influence dynamics, but is unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Design Of An Efficient Tunable Dual Narrow-band Mems Mid And Far Ir Emitter With Me-NTA For Industrial And Biomedical Applications
authors: Md. Imran Hasmi, Md. Saffat Gohor, Foez Ahmed, Jaker Hossain
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05838v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spectrally selective infrared (IR) thermal emitters are gaining much attention now-a-days for sensing, spectroscopy and biomedical applications. In this research, two metasurface incorporated IR emitters are proposed and numerically analyzed using finite element method (FEM). First structure comprises a NiCr heater integrated with a NiCr-based metallic nanotube array (Me-NTA) metasurface to produce a single-narrowband emission in the mid-infrared (MIR) region. Furthermore, an Au-based Me-NTA metasurface on a NiCr-Au hybrid heater subsequently produces dual-narrowband emission in the short-and far-infrared (SIR and FIR) spectrums. Function of these emitters can be explained by Joule heating with the help of DC bias and consequently uniform temperature distribution can be observed along the active region. Simulation analysis shows that NiCr-metasurface based emitter produces single narrow-band near perfect emission centered at 4.5 {\mu}m in MIR region at an operating temperature of 700 K with maximum in-band conversion efficiency (CE) of 32.3% and radiated power of 199 mW. On the other hand, Au-metasurface based emitter generates dual-narrowband emission peaking at 2.5 {\mu}m and 10 {\mu}m, correlating to SIR and FIR subsequently, achieving maximum emission of 93% and 85%, respectively. The in-band CE for this emitter attains 10.4% and 4.4% in the first and second bands, associated with radiated powers of 350 mW and 147 mW, accordingly. Furthermore, execution of the emitter at 500 K reveals FIR emission with reduced power consumption. These results substantiate the possibilities of the suggested emitters in various industrial and biomedical applications.
tldr: This paper designs and simulates MEMS-based metasurface infrared emitters for narrowband thermal emission in mid- and far-IR, targeting industrial and biomedical sensing applications.
motivation: To develop spectrally selective IR emitters with high efficiency for sensing, spectroscopy, and biomedical applications.
method: Finite element method (FEM) simulations of two metasurface designs: NiCr-based metallic nanotube array (Me-NTA) for single-band MIR emission, and Au-based Me-NTA on NiCr-Au hybrid heater for dual-band SIR/FIR emission.
result: NiCr emitter achieves 32.3% conversion efficiency at 4.5 μm; Au emitter achieves 93% and 85% emission at 2.5 μm and 10 μm with 10.4% and 4.4% in-band efficiency.
conclusion: The proposed emitters show potential for industrial and biomedical applications, but the paper focuses on device engineering with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Inverse Design Of Realizable Metasurface Based Absorbers Using Improved Conditioning And Diversity Enhanced Progressively Growing GANs
authors: Vineetha Joy, Mohammad Abdullah, Pramit Pal, Anshuman Kumar, Amit Sethi, Hema Singh
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05849v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Metasurfaces enable precise manipulation of electromagnetic waves for applications such as beam steering, sensing, and stealth technology. However, inverse design of metasurfaces with targeted EM responses remains challenging due to the computational expense of iterative full wave simulation driven optimization and the limited conditioning fidelity and diversity of existing generative approaches. To address these challenges, this paper presents a generative inverse design framework for controllable and physically consistent metasurface synthesis under continuous spectral constraints. The proposed approach employs a progressively growing Wasserstein generative adversarial network with gradient penalty integrated with feature wise linear modulation based conditioning for stable propagation of continuous spectral and fabrication constraints. EM consistency is embedded directly into the generative learning process through a surrogate assisted spectral alignment loss, enabling physics constrained generation during training. Further, a determinantal point process based diversity regularization strategy is incorporated to generate geometrically diverse yet spectrally consistent realizations for the same target response. The effectiveness of the proposed framework is demonstrated through the generation of practically realizable metasurface absorbers exhibiting diverse reflection characteristics in the frequency range of 2 to 18 GHz. EM simulations validate that the generated designs meet the target specifications with high accuracy. The final proposed framework achieved an average mean squared error of 0.0052, diversity score of 0.8730, band alignment accuracy of 0.8533, and a valid EM design generation percentage of 89.57, clearly demonstrating its capability to generate highly accurate, diverse, electromagnetically consistent and fabrication realizable metasurface configurations.
tldr: This paper presents a generative inverse design framework using progressively growing GANs for metasurface absorbers, focusing on electromagnetic wave manipulation.
motivation: Inverse design of metasurfaces is computationally expensive and existing generative models lack fidelity and diversity; the authors aim to address these challenges.
method: A progressively growing Wasserstein GAN with gradient penalty, feature-wise linear modulation conditioning, surrogate-assisted spectral alignment loss, and determinantal point process diversity regularization.
result: The framework achieves high accuracy (MSE 0.0052), diversity (0.8730), band alignment (0.8533), and 89.57% valid EM designs for metasurface absorbers in 2-18 GHz.
conclusion: The approach enables efficient generation of diverse, physically consistent, and fabrication-realizable metasurface designs, with potential for broader EM applications.

title: Euler Scheme For Stochastic Functional Differential Equations Driven By Fractional Brownian Motion Via Fractional Calculus Techniques
authors: Alexander Abreu (CIMFAV), H\'ector Araya (UNAI), Lisandro Fermin (AMSE), Johanna Garz\'on (UNAL), Soledad Torres
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05195v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a stochastic functional differential equation (SFDE) with memory driven by a fractional Brownian motion (fBm) with Hurst parameter H>1/2. An Euler-type numerical scheme is proposed and analyzed under suitable regularity conditions on the drift and diffusion coefficients using tools from fractional calculus. We prove the convergence of the scheme and derive the corresponding rate in terms of the discretization step. Numerical simulations illustrate the theoretical results and confirm the accuracy of the proposed method.
tldr: This paper develops an Euler numerical scheme for stochastic functional differential equations driven by fractional Brownian motion with Hurst parameter > 1/2, using fractional calculus techniques.
motivation: To provide a convergent numerical method for SFDEs with memory driven by fBm, which are important in modeling systems with long-range dependence.
method: An Euler-type scheme is proposed and analyzed under regularity conditions on drift and diffusion coefficients, using tools from fractional calculus to handle the fBm.
result: Convergence of the scheme is proved and the rate in terms of discretization step is derived; numerical simulations confirm accuracy.

title: Pseudosymmetry, Ricci Soliton And Curvature Inheritance Symmetries Of Friedmann Lema\^itre Robertson Walker Spacetime
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05207v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Friedmann--Lema\^{i}tre--Robertson--Walker (FLRW) spacetime, which was first proposed by Friedmann (1922--1924) and Lema\^{i}tre (1927) and subsequently developed by Robertson and Walker (1935), is an isotropic and homogeneous cosmological model of the universe. A thorough analysis of Ricci solitons and curvature inheritance properties reveals that the spacetime admits almost Ricci soliton and [MATH]-Ricci Yamabe soliton structures with respect to the non-Killing soliton vector fields [MATH] and [MATH]. title: Entropy-Compatible Barrier Schemes For Diffusive Fene Flows

title: The Euclidean Algorithm, Lotuses And Singularities
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05211v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The anthyphairetic process leads from a pair (a,b) of coprime positive integers to the pair (1,1) by successive subtractions of the smaller number from the bigger one. This process, which is a slow version of Euclid's algorithm applied to the pair (a,b), corresponds naturally to the process of successive blowups leading to the minimal embedded resolution of the plane curve defined by y^a - x^b = 0. This blowup process may be represented graphically by a special two-dimensional simplicial complex called a lotus. This allows to localize the various numbers appearing either during the anthyphairetic process or during the Euclidean algorithm at precise positions inside the lotus. In this introductory article, I recall first the construction of this lotus starting from the sequence of quotients generated by the Euclidean algorithm. I present then an alternative way of constructing it directly from the sequence of pairs of coprime integers generated by the anthyphairetic process, using what I call anthyphairetic rectangles. I conclude by explaining how to reconstruct from a lotus the corresponding sequence of pairs of coprime integers. This is a simple illustration of the way lotuses may serve as computational architectures.
tldr: This paper explores a geometric interpretation of the Euclidean algorithm using lotuses and singularities of plane curves, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To provide a visual and combinatorial framework for understanding the Euclidean algorithm and its relation to algebraic geometry.
method: The paper constructs a two-dimensional simplicial complex (lotus) from the sequence of quotients in the Euclidean algorithm, and introduces anthyphairetic rectangles as an alternative construction.
result: The lotus encodes the anthyphairetic process and the Euclidean algorithm, allowing localization of numbers and reconstruction of coprime pairs.
conclusion: Lotuses serve as computational architectures for number theory, but the work is purely mathematical and unrelated to the user's research interests.

title: Umbral Methods, Function Factorisation And Generalisation Of The Fourier Transform Method

abstract: ArXiv:2606.05213v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a systematic way to construct trigonometric-like functions beyond the classical sine--cosine pair by factorising rational umbral operators. For each integer [MATH], the construction produces [MATH] functions which play the role of higher-order trigonometric components: their sum reconstructs the corresponding umbral function, while the individual components isolate the different cyclic sectors of its expansion. The construction is developed first in the formal umbral setting. The quadratic case [MATH] gives the Gaussian trigonometric functions, in which the cosine-like component is a Gaussian and the sine-like component is its natural umbral companion. The cubic case [MATH] yields a three-component cyclic system and shows how the same idea extends beyond the usual even--odd decomposition. These examples suggest that trigonometric factorisation is not restricted to ordinary rotations, but belongs to a broader cyclic principle in umbral calculus. We then reinterpret the same formal identities through the recently developed analytic umbral framework. In this second step, the cyclic components are realised by Mellin--Barnes pairings, and the root-of-unity decomposition is related to the splitting of the corresponding spectral kernel. This analytic formulation provides contour representations, local expansions, and sectorial asymptotics for the functions obtained formally. Finally, we indicate how the same cyclic kernels act on Fourier transforms. motivation: To extend the concept of trigonometric functions beyond the classical sine-cosine pair by exploiting factorisation in umbral calculus, aiming to uncover a broader cyclic principle.
method: The authors first define higher-order trigonometric functions through factorisation of rational umbral operators in a formal umbral setting, then reinterpret these identities using analytic umbral calculus with Mellin-Barnes pairings and root-of-unity decompositions.

title: Analytic Umbral Transmutations And Bessel Moments
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05214v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop an analytic umbral approach to Bessel moments, using them as a concrete testbed justifying the passage from formal indicial umbral calculus to Mellin--Barnes umbral transmutation theory. The cubic moment provides the basic example [...] We show that this obstruction is removed by replacing the purely formal expansion with an analytic umbral transmutation. In this setting, exponential umbral pairings are interpreted through Mellin--Barnes integrals, and Ramanujan's Master Theorem acts as an inverse selection principle for the spectral ground state, or clock, associated with a given Bessel product. The factorisation \(J_0^3=J_0J_0^2\) produces two distinct clocks and reduces the cubic full-line moment to a one-dimensional Barnes integral, equivalently to a Meijer \(G\)-function. This gives the classical value of the cubic Bessel moment and clarifies why the divergent Appell realisation is only a local representation of a globally meaningful umbral identity. The same mechanism is then applied to scaled cubic products and to the fourth Bessel moment. [...] The fifth moment marks the first genuinely higher-rank case: the natural umbral grouping leads to a bivariate Barnes transmutation rather than to an ordinary Meijer \(G\)-function. motivation: To resolve convergence issues in formal umbral expansions for Bessel moments and provide a rigorous analytic framework.

title: Bounded Deep Unfolding For Joint Beamforming And Scheduling In Multi-Cell Mimo Networks
authors: Jiansheng Li, Shuqi Chai, Fan Xu, Kaiming Shen, Guangxu Zhu, Junting Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05246v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates the joint resource block group (RBG) scheduling and beamforming optimization problem for weighted sum-rate (WSR) maximization in multi-cell multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) downlink networks. While the Fast Fractional Programming (FastFP) framework provides a reliable model-driven solution, it suffers from conservative continuous beamforming updates and prohibitive computational overhead during the discrete RBG matching phase. To address these bottlenecks, we propose a joint deep unfolding framework comprising two core modules: P-Net and K-Net. For continuous beamforming, P-Net learns an adaptive relaxation factor along the analytical FastFP update direction. By strictly constraining this factor within an ascent-preserving interval, P-Net accelerates the optimization trajectory while rigorously retaining monotonic improvement and stationary-point convergence guarantees. For discrete RBG scheduling, K-Net learns a long-horizon priority policy that guides a low-complexity greedy assignment, effectively preserving the assignment quality while bypassing the high complexity of Hungarian matching. Both networks leverage analytical algorithmic priors and utilize recurrent parameter sharing, enabling flexible inference beyond the training horizon. Extensive simulations demonstrate that the proposed joint framework achieves higher WSR and faster execution times than conventional model-driven baselines, while generalizing robustly across unseen network scales, antenna configurations, and channel conditions without retraining.
tldr: This paper proposes a deep unfolding framework for joint beamforming and scheduling in multi-cell MIMO networks to maximize weighted sum-rate.
motivation: Existing model-driven solutions like FastFP suffer from conservative updates and high computational overhead in discrete scheduling.
method: Two neural modules (P-Net and K-Net) are integrated into the FastFP algorithm: P-Net learns an adaptive relaxation factor for beamforming updates, and K-Net learns a priority policy for greedy scheduling.
result: The proposed framework achieves higher weighted sum-rate and faster execution than conventional baselines, and generalizes to unseen network scales and configurations.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that deep unfolding with algorithmic priors can improve both performance and efficiency in wireless network optimization.

title: X-Band UAV-enabled Integrated Sensing And Communications For Vehicular Networks
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05262v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Uncrewed aerial vehicles (UAVs) are increasingly considered as aerial platforms capable of providing both sensing and communication services, representing a promising paradigm for intelligent transportation systems. This paper investigates the optimal time allocation for a UAV-enabled integrated sensing and communication (ISaC) system operating in the X-band for vehicular networks. We analyze the trade-off between sensing accuracy and communication performance under practical UAV constraints and fading effects, considering both single-shadowing and double-shadowing channel models. An optimization framework is developed to allocate time between sensing and communication while guaranteeing minimum communication rates and sufficient sensing reliability. Simulation results demonstrate adaptive time allocation strategies, highlighting how UAV-to-ground channel conditions and target distances influence the balance between sensing and communication in smart mobility scenarios.
tldr: This paper studies time allocation for UAV-based integrated sensing and communication in vehicular networks, focusing on X-band performance under fading channels.
motivation: To optimize the trade-off between sensing and communication in UAV-enabled systems for intelligent transportation.
method: An optimization framework for time allocation between sensing and communication, considering single- and double-shadowing channel models.
result: Adaptive time allocation strategies depend on UAV-to-ground channel conditions and target distances.
conclusion: The work provides insights for balancing sensing and communication in smart mobility, but is not directly related to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Learning Implicit Feasibility Constraints For Real-World Routing And Scheduling: Application To Log Transportation
authors: Abdelhakim Abdellaoui, Ayoub Boufous, Issmail El Hallaoui, Loubna Benabbou, Francois Aub\'e, Mouloud Amazouz
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05353v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Real-world vehicle routing and scheduling problems involve complex operational rules and feasibility constraints typically formulated as mixed-integer linear programs (MILP). However, optimization tools are built around a fixed set of hard-coded constraints, while in practice this set evolves as new rules or preferences emerge, seasonally or permanently. Updating it requires modeling and operations research skills that planners rarely have, so generated plans are routinely adjusted by hand based on practical knowledge. Building on recent work that uses machine learning to recover such hidden constraints, we propose a data-driven constraint-learning approach that trains three complementary predictors, a Graph Neural Network (GNN), a decision tree, and a linear regression, on historical execution data from a log-truck routing and scheduling problem ([MATH]), and embeds each inside a MILP through linearized constraints. We further introduce a stacking mechanism that combines all three within a single augmented optimization problem (AOP), letting the solver endogenously select the most reliable predictor for each decision. On real-world industrial data, each predictor already improves feasibility, but the stacked embedding consistently achieves the lowest objective degradation: it (i)~satisfies the operational rules on unseen instances with smaller degradation than any single-model variant, (ii)~picks the most appropriate predictor per decision without prior knowledge of the rule's nature, and (iii)~reduces daily manual adjustment effort while remaining tractable for daily use. tldr: This paper uses machine learning to learn implicit feasibility constraints for log-truck routing and scheduling, embedding predictors into a MILP to reduce manual adjustments.
motivation: Real-world vehicle routing problems have evolving operational rules that are hard to update in optimization tools, leading to manual plan adjustments.
method: Trains a GNN, decision tree, and linear regression on historical data to predict feasibility, then embeds them as linearized constraints in a MILP, with a stacking mechanism to select the best predictor per decision.
result: The stacked embedding achieves the lowest objective degradation while satisfying operational rules on unseen instances, reducing manual adjustment effort.
conclusion: The framework enables optimization tools to adapt to evolving practice without manual remodeling, with potential applications beyond log transportation.

title: Bayesian Equilibria Of Heterogeneous Non-Atomic Routing Games With Private Information

title: Sequence Reconstruction For Substitution Channel: New Sufficient Conditions And Algorithms

title: A Two-Channel F-Transform Representation For Early Trajectory Characterization In Iterated Correlation Dynamics
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05462v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Many nonlinear iterative procedures generate high-dimensional trajectories whose early behavior is informative but difficult to compare directly. This paper studies a soft-computing representation problem: how to convert a short early trajectory segment into compact, interpretable, fixed-dimensional fuzzy coordinates that preserve information about subsequent convergence and trajectory geometry. The problem is investigated for iterated Pearson correlation matrices, a nonlinear matrix iteration historically connected with CONCOR-type blockmodeling and repeated-correlation methods. The proposed descriptor uses two logarithmic signals from the early post-transient regime: a step-size signal, measuring contraction magnitude, and a contraction-ratio signal, measuring local contraction evolution. Each signal is projected onto a three-node triangular fuzzy partition using zero-degree F-transform coefficients and one centered first-degree coefficient. This yields an eight-dimensional two-channel representation separating local level from local trend and contraction magnitude from contraction evolution. Across 22 matrix dimensions with 1000 trajectories per dimension, the descriptor is compared with raw trajectory samples, statistical summaries, and PCA-compressed raw features using Random Forest regression for convergence-length approximation. method: Two logarithmic signals (step-size and contraction-ratio) from the early post-transient regime are projected onto a three-node triangular fuzzy partition using zero-degree and first-degree F-transform coefficients, producing an eight-dimensional two-channel representation. conclusion: The proposed representation offers a compact and interpretable alternative for early trajectory characterization, with potential applications in soft computing and data analysis, though its relevance to quantum information or thermodynamics is indirect.

title: Optimal Experimental Design For Passive Imaging Source Problems
authors: Christian Aarset, Thorsten Hohage, Georg Stadler
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05490v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work focuses on optimal experimental design (OED) methods for passive imaging. We adopt a Bayesian inverse problem framework for passive imaging source problems, primarily focusing on spatially uncorrelated sources and systems governed by the Helmholtz equation. title: Robust Repair Of Reed-Solomon Codes

authors: Yixuan Li, Jun Wang, Hongbo Xu, Ji Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05600v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates a rotatable antenna (RA)-enabled uplink non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) system, where a base station equipped with multiple independently RAs serves both ground and aerial users. Specifically, we formulate an energy efficiency (EE) maximization problem by jointly optimizing receive beamforming, user power allocation, and RA rotation. To make the problem tractable, a new block coordinate descent-based algorithm is developed, in which the receive beamforming is updated via the minimum mean square error criterion, while the power allocation and RA rotation are handled by fractional programming and successive convex approximation. Numerical results demonstrate the EE superiority of the proposed RA-NOMA scheme over several benchmarks.
tldr: This paper optimizes energy efficiency in a rotatable antenna-enabled uplink NOMA system, focusing on wireless communication rather than quantum or thermodynamic topics.
motivation: To improve energy efficiency in wireless systems with rotatable antennas and NOMA, addressing joint optimization of beamforming, power allocation, and antenna rotation.
method: A block coordinate descent algorithm is developed, using MMSE for beamforming, fractional programming for power allocation, and successive convex approximation for antenna rotation.
result: The proposed RA-NOMA scheme achieves superior energy efficiency compared to benchmarks.
conclusion: The work demonstrates the potential of rotatable antennas in NOMA systems for energy-efficient communication, with implications for future wireless networks.

title: Asymmetry Of Entropy Invariants For Generic Mixing $Z^n$-Actions
authors: Valery V. Ryzhikov Mikhail V. Engelgardt
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05619v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Suppose that for a mixing [MATH]-action, [MATH], there exists a Kirillov-Kushnirenko entropy that is zero for this action and completely positive for its inverse. We prove that this property is generic for the mixing [MATH]-actions.
tldr: The paper proves that for generic mixing Z^n-actions, the Kirillov-Kushnirenko entropy can be zero for the action and completely positive for its inverse, demonstrating asymmetry of entropy invariants.
motivation: To understand the behavior of entropy invariants under mixing actions and their inverses, specifically exploring asymmetry properties.
method: The authors use ergodic theory and generic arguments for mixing Z^n-actions, likely involving Baire category or measure-theoretic genericity.
result: It is shown that the property of having zero entropy for the action and completely positive entropy for its inverse is generic among mixing Z^n-actions.
conclusion: This reveals a fundamental asymmetry in entropy invariants for mixing actions, with implications for the classification of dynamical systems.

title: Iterative Thresholding Pursuit With Continuation For $\ell_{1-2}$-Regularized Sparse Recovery
authors: Junxi Wu, Zeyu Dong, Jun-Feng Yin
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05657v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sparse recovery aims to reconstruct sparse signals from underdetermined and possibly noisy linear measurements. Existing [MATH] iterative thresholding schemes are first-order methods. We propose an iterative thresholding pursuit method with continuation (ITP-C) for [MATH]-regularized sparse recovery. The method goes beyond first-order thresholding by combining the active-set identification capability of the [MATH] proximal step with a restricted least-squares pursuit step that provides a second-order update on the identified support. The support is generated adaptively by the thresholding update, and no prior knowledge of the true sparsity level is required. To control the possible instability of the pursuit step while preserving the descent structure of the continuation scheme, we impose a strict descent check with respect to the dynamic objective. We establish convergence of the generated sequence under the Kurdyka-Lojasiewicz framework and prove a local oracle-type property after correct support identification. Numerical experiments on synthetic sparse recovery and image reconstruction illustrate the descent preservation of the proposed safeguard and demonstrate the improved recovery performance of ITP-C over the state-of-the-art baselines.
tldr: This paper proposes an iterative thresholding pursuit method with continuation for ℓ1-2 regularized sparse recovery, improving upon first-order methods by combining active-set identification with a second-order pursuit step.
motivation: Existing iterative thresholding schemes are first-order methods that may converge slowly or inaccurately for sparse recovery problems. The authors aim to develop a more efficient algorithm that leverages second-order updates on the identified support.
method: The method (ITP-C) combines a proximal step for active-set identification with a restricted least-squares pursuit step for second-order update on the support. A strict descent check with respect to the dynamic objective ensures stability, and convergence is analyzed under the Kurdyka-Lojasiewicz framework.
result: Numerical experiments on synthetic sparse recovery and image reconstruction show that ITP-C outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in recovery performance while preserving descent properties.
conclusion: The proposed algorithm offers improved sparse recovery performance and theoretical convergence guarantees, with potential applications in signal processing and image reconstruction.

title: Sparse Recovery Via $\ell_1^2-\eta\ell_2^2$ Minimization
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05674v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The weighted difference of squared norms (WDSN) penalty [MATH] with [MATH] has attracted considerable attention due to its strong sparsity-promoting ability and favorable reconstruction performance in compressed sensing and inverse problems. However, exact recovery guarantees and restricted isometry property (RIP) analysis for WDSN minimization have not yet been established. In this paper, we address this gap. First, we establish sufficient conditions for the exact recovery of [MATH]-sparse signals based on the null space property (NSP). Then, under the [MATH]-RIP condition, we derive stable recovery guarantees for both [MATH]-sparse signals and general signals, and characterize upper bounds on the reconstruction error. Furthermore, we propose a WDSN-based regularized model to handle both noiseless and noisy observations in a unified framework. To design an efficient algorithm, we derive an explicit formula for the proximal operator of the WDSN functional. Based on this proximal solver, we develop a suitable variable-splitting scheme within the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) and establish its global convergence under some mild conditions. Finally, numerical experiments show that the proposed method outperforms the iterative half variation method in both noiseless and noisy sparse recovery tasks.
tldr: This paper establishes theoretical recovery guarantees for sparse signal reconstruction using a weighted difference of squared norms penalty in compressed sensing.
motivation: To fill the gap in exact recovery guarantees and RIP analysis for WDSN minimization, which is known for strong sparsity promotion.
method: Derives sufficient conditions via null space property and stable recovery guarantees under RIP, then develops an ADMM algorithm using the proximal operator of the WDSN functional.
result: Provides theoretical bounds on reconstruction error and demonstrates numerically that the method outperforms iterative half variation in sparse recovery tasks.
conclusion: The work offers a rigorous foundation for WDSN minimization and an efficient algorithm, with potential applications in compressed sensing and inverse problems.

title: Local Increment Inference For Time-inhomogeneous Drift In Gaussian Processes
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05681v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study statistical inference for deterministic drift structures in Gaussian process models under high-frequency observations.The observed process consists of a centered stationary Gaussian component combined with a broad class of time-inhomogeneous deterministic drifts. To estimate the drift parameter, we introduce a least squares-type contrast based on first-order increments. We establish consistency and asymptotic normality under weak dependence conditions on the Gaussian component. A central feature of the framework is that the rate of convergence of the estimator depends jointly on the local roughness of the Gaussian noise and the long-time information accumulation structure generated by the drift. The theory accommodates a wide range of drift families, including integrable, polynomial-type, and periodic structures. In particular, different drift densities produce qualitatively different statistical regimes, including non-standard rates of convergence and accelerated rates for persistent or growing deterministic structures.
tldr: This paper studies statistical inference for deterministic drift in Gaussian processes under high-frequency observations, focusing on asymptotic properties of a least squares-type estimator.
motivation: To develop inference methods for time-inhomogeneous drift in Gaussian processes, which is important for applications like signal processing and financial modeling.
method: Introduces a least squares-type contrast based on first-order increments and establishes consistency and asymptotic normality under weak dependence conditions.
result: The convergence rate depends on local roughness of the Gaussian noise and long-time information accumulation; different drift families yield non-standard and accelerated rates.
conclusion: Provides a theoretical framework for drift estimation in Gaussian processes, with implications for statistical inference in non-stationary settings.

title: Bv Construction Of Susy Vertex Algebras From Susy Factorization Algebras
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05706v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct [MATH] supersymmetric (SUSY) vertex algebras from supersymmetric enhancements of Costello--Gwilliam factorization algebras on super Riemann surfaces. Introducing SUSY factorization algebras defined on embedded SUSY disks together with natural symmetry conditions, we prove a SUSY analogue of the Costello--Gwilliam extraction theorem. As an application, we study the holomorphic sigma model in the BV formalism. For a linear target, we obtain the free [MATH]-[MATH] system and recover its structure as a SUSY vertex algebra. For general complex targets, we describe the descent of the theory under coordinate changes and identify the resulting SUSY vertex algebra with the chiral de Rham complex. We further show that Ricci-flat K\"ahler and hyperk\"ahler targets give rise to [MATH] and [MATH] supersymmetric enhancements introduced by Ben-Zvi--Heluani--Szczesny.
tldr: This paper constructs supersymmetric vertex algebras from supersymmetric factorization algebras on super Riemann surfaces, focusing on the BV formalism and chiral de Rham complex.
motivation: To extend the Costello-Gwilliam extraction theorem to the supersymmetric setting and to understand the algebraic structures underlying supersymmetric field theories.
method: The authors define SUSY factorization algebras on embedded SUSY disks with symmetry conditions and prove a SUSY analogue of the extraction theorem, then apply it to holomorphic sigma models.
result: For linear targets, the free β-γ system is recovered; for general complex targets, the resulting SUSY vertex algebra is identified with the chiral de Rham complex; Ricci-flat Kähler and hyperkähler targets yield N=1 and N=2 supersymmetric enhancements.
conclusion: The work provides a rigorous construction of SUSY vertex algebras from factorization algebras, with implications for the algebraic structure of supersymmetric field theories and potential connections to string theory.

title: Direct Reconstruction For Acoustic Inverse Born Scattering
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05977v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the inverse medium scattering problem for the Helmholtz equation in two dimensions, i.e., the task to recover a compactly supported penetrable two-dimensional scatterer from full knowledge of the associated far field data or, equivalently, the far field operator. Although this problem is uniquely solvable, it is severely ill-posed and nonlinear. In the regime of weak scattering, the Born approximation yields a linearized relation between the contrast and the far field data, thus overcoming the second difficulty. This linear setting allows to build on recent work on linearized electrical impedance tomography, which relies on triangular Zernike decompositions, to derive an explicit reconstruction formula that expresses the expansion coefficients of the contrast in terms of those of the far field data. By choosing the expansion functions appropriately, the resulting system matrix decouples into separate (infinite) triangular systems for the spatial angular frequencies in the contrast. Consequently, each of these systems can be solved independently by performing forward substitutions. Our numerical experiments indicate that this approach, combined with an adequate regularization method, remains effective even when applied to full nonlinear far field data beyond the Born regime.
tldr: This paper presents a direct reconstruction method for the acoustic inverse Born scattering problem using triangular Zernike decompositions.
motivation: To overcome the nonlinearity and ill-posedness of the inverse medium scattering problem for the Helmholtz equation.
method: The Born approximation linearizes the problem, then triangular Zernike decompositions are used to derive an explicit reconstruction formula that decouples the system into independent triangular systems solved by forward substitution.
result: Numerical experiments show the method remains effective even beyond the Born regime when combined with regularization.
conclusion: The approach provides a fast, direct reconstruction algorithm for acoustic scattering, with potential extensions to other inverse problems.

title: Search-Time Contamination In Deep Research Agents: Measuring Performance Inflation In Public Benchmark Evaluation
authors: Yongjie Wang, Xinyue Zhang, Kunhong Yao, Zhiwei Zeng, Kaisong Song, Jun Lin, Zhiqi Shen
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05241v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Public benchmarks enable fair and reproducible evaluation of LLM reasoning, but they become fragile for deep research agents that actively search the web during inference. Such agents may retrieve public benchmark metadata, question context, or even ground-truth answers via web search. This gives rise to Search-Time Contamination (STC), where external retrieval bypasses intended reasoning and inflates measured performance. We systematically study STC in deep research agent evaluation. We define three contamination types with increasing severity, namely Benchmark Metadata Leakage, Question-Context Leakage, and Explicit Answer Leakage, and develop detection algorithms to identify them and quantify their impact on agent performance. Evaluating modern deep research agents on six public benchmarks, we find that STC is widespread and can inflate performance by up to 4%. Our findings show that existing evaluations may overestimate true reasoning ability. We therefore advocate contamination-aware practices, including isolated sandboxes, transparent search trajectories, and controlled benchmark access.
tldr: This paper studies how deep research agents can inflate benchmark scores by retrieving answers via web search during inference, a phenomenon called Search-Time Contamination.
motivation: Public benchmarks are widely used to evaluate LLM reasoning, but deep research agents that search the web during inference may inadvertently access benchmark data, leading to overestimated performance.
method: The authors define three types of contamination (metadata leakage, question-context leakage, explicit answer leakage) and develop detection algorithms to identify and quantify contamination in agent evaluations.
result: Experiments on six public benchmarks show that STC is widespread and can inflate performance by up to 4%.
conclusion: The findings highlight the need for contamination-aware evaluation practices such as isolated sandboxes, transparent search trajectories, and controlled benchmark access.

title: Should Demand Models Incorporate Competitor Prices? Oblivious Learning And Algorithmic Collusion
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05363v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: On a platform with many sellers, should a pricing algorithm explicitly model competitors' prices when learning demand? Classical learning arguments suggest an affirmative answer: ignoring competitors induces model misspecification and inefficiency. In contrast, recent work on algorithmic collusion suggests that strategic obliviousness -- deliberately ignoring competitor prices -- may facilitate collusive outcomes and improve profits. We study this modeling choice in a stylized competitive market with unknown noisy demand, in which multiple sellers repeatedly set prices and estimate demand via iterated least squares, and either incorporate competitors' prices into their demand models (informed) or ignore them (oblivious). We first show that, relative to a monopolist, an oblivious seller in a competitive market must explore more aggressively to compensate for the loss of dynamic competitor information. Building on this insight, we characterize market dynamics when all sellers are oblivious and show that prices converge to the competitive outcome under sufficient exploration, while a continuum of pseudo-equilibria arises when exploration decays. Analyzing the resulting price trajectories, we uncover an excursion phenomenon that gives rise to transient collusive patterns that dissipate as learning progresses. In markets with both oblivious and informed sellers, the informed strictly out-earn the oblivious. Read as a strategy game, the modeling choice has a unique Nash equilibrium: the all-informed market, in which prices converge to the competitive outcome efficiently. Overall, our results indicate that collusive patterns are not robust and are not sustained by oblivious modeling; therefore, incorporating competitor information, together with sufficient price exploration, remains a reliable strategy for sellers in competitive markets.
tldr: This paper studies whether pricing algorithms should incorporate competitor prices in a competitive market, finding that informed models outperform oblivious ones and collusive patterns are not robust.
motivation: To resolve the tension between classical learning arguments favoring informed models and recent work suggesting obliviousness may facilitate collusion.
method: The authors model a stylized competitive market with multiple sellers using iterated least squares to estimate demand, comparing oblivious and informed pricing strategies.
result: Oblivious sellers require more aggressive exploration; all-oblivious markets converge to competitive outcomes under sufficient exploration but exhibit transient collusive patterns; informed sellers outperform oblivious ones.
conclusion: Incorporating competitor information with sufficient price exploration is a reliable strategy; collusive patterns from obliviousness are not robust.

title: Willing But Unable: Separating Refusal From Capability In Code LLMs Via Abliteration
authors: Cristina Carleo, Pietro Liguori, Naghmeh Ivaki, Domenico Cotroneo
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05396v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Producing a labeled vulnerable code at scale is a recurring obstacle for learning-based vulnerability detection: mined corpora carry substantial label noise, and existing LLM-based augmentation propagates these inaccuracies because it transforms vulnerable seeds rather than synthesising vulnerabilities from a specification. A complementary route is to start from safe code and ask an instruction-tuned LLM to inject a specified CWE (which would shift the labeling burden from open-ended detection to bounded binary confirmation) but safety-aligned code LLMs systematically refuse such prompts. This paper is a preliminary feasibility study of abliteration, a low-rank weight edit that orthogonally projects out the refusal direction in the residual stream, as a tool to remove this barrier. We use Python and CWE-89 (SQL injection) as a case study, evaluating the Qwen2.5-Coder-Instruct family at 3B, 7B, and 14B parameters on safe samples drawn from PromSec and SafeCoder, replicated three times per condition. We find that (i) refusal on injection prompts is strongly size- and prompt-context-dependent: the 14B refuses 100% of prompts, the 7B refuses 73% of PromSec but only 5% of SafeCoder, whereas the 3B is essentially never blocked; (ii) abliteration reduces refusal to zero or near-zero across all sizes while leaving syntactic validity above 93%, supporting the view that, in this setting, refusal can be detached from measured code-generation capability; and (iii) the post-abliteration injection rate remains capacity-bound (88-97% on the 14B, 89-90% on the 7B, and 25-48% on the 3B) separating willingness, which abliteration unlocks, from capability, which scales with parameters. Vulnerability verdicts are produced by a three-tool detector ensemble (CodeQL, Semgrep, Bandit) followed by manual adjudication by two authors on detector-positive outputs.
tldr: This paper explores abliteration, a weight-editing technique to bypass safety alignment in code LLMs for vulnerability injection, but is unrelated to the user's research interests.
motivation: To enable instruction-tuned code LLMs to inject specific vulnerabilities (CWEs) into safe code for generating labeled vulnerable datasets, overcoming refusal due to safety alignment.
method: Applied abliteration (low-rank weight edit projecting out the refusal direction) to Qwen2.5-Coder-Instruct models (3B, 7B, 14B) and evaluated injection success on safe samples from PromSec and SafeCoder.
result: Abliteration reduced refusal to near-zero while maintaining syntactic validity >93%; injection rate scaled with model size (14B: 88-97%, 7B: 89-90%, 3B: 25-48%).
conclusion: Refusal can be separated from code-generation capability; abliteration enables vulnerability injection but capability remains a bottleneck.

title: Rh+: Row-Hit-Optimized Scheduling For PIM-based Llm Inference
authors: Yongchan Jung, Shafayat Mowla Anik, Byeong Kil Lee, Jeeho Ryoo
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05511v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language model inference on processing-in-memory (PIM) architectures promises to break the memory wall by performing multiply-accumulate (MAC) operations directly within HBM3 DRAM banks. Prior work identifies the power constraint timing parameter nCCDAB as the primary performance bottleneck and optimizes scheduling accordingly. We demonstrate that for GEMV operations that dominate autoregressive decoding, the DRAM row cycle time (nRC) is 10 to 11 times larger than nCCDAB. Consequently, nCCDAB is entirely masked, rendering prior nCCDAB-focused optimizations ineffective for these workloads. The root cause is inherited host-centric address interleaving, which forces every all-bank MAC command into a different DRAM row. We propose RH+ scheduling, a simple stride change that keeps 32 consecutive MAC operations within the same row. Cycle-accurate simulation across four LLM workloads shows that RH+ delivers 8-12x speedup, over 74% energy reduction, and up to 52x EDP improvement.
tldr: This paper proposes a row-hit scheduling optimization for processing-in-memory architectures to accelerate LLM inference, but it is unrelated to the user's research interests in quantum information and thermodynamics.
motivation: Prior PIM scheduling focused on nCCDAB timing, but for GEMV operations in LLM decoding, nRC is the dominant bottleneck due to host-centric address interleaving.
method: The authors identify the row cycle time (nRC) as the key bottleneck and propose RH+ scheduling, a stride change that keeps 32 consecutive MAC operations in the same DRAM row.
result: Cycle-accurate simulation shows 8-12x speedup, over 74% energy reduction, and up to 52x EDP improvement across four LLM workloads.
conclusion: RH+ scheduling effectively mitigates the row activation overhead for PIM-based LLM inference, but the work is purely classical and does not intersect with quantum computing or thermodynamics.

title: Dimensionality Reduction For Cyberattack Classification: A Comparative Evaluation Of Pca And Linear Predictive Coding
authors: Nelly Elsayed, Zag Elsayed, Navid Asadizanjani
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05584v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: High-dimensional feature representations are widely used in machine learning-based cyberattack detection systems. However, they increase computational complexity and may hinder deployment in resource-constrained environments.
