In this paper, we investigate feature compression techniques for cyberattack classification by comparing two dimensionality reduction approaches: Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and Linear Predictive Coding (LPC). Compressed feature representations with varying dimensionalities are generated and evaluated across several classification models. Experimental analysis demonstrates that PCA preserves classification performance even under aggressive compression. On the other hand, LPC provides competitive predictive representations with slightly larger performance degradation. The results show that substantial reductions in feature dimensionality can be achieved with minimal impact on classification accuracy, highlighting the potential of lightweight feature compression for efficient cybersecurity analytics.
tldr: This paper compares PCA and LPC for dimensionality reduction in cyberattack classification, finding that PCA preserves accuracy under aggressive compression.
motivation: High-dimensional features in cyberattack detection increase computational complexity, hindering deployment in resource-constrained environments.
method: The authors apply PCA and LPC to compress feature representations and evaluate classification performance across several models.
result: PCA maintains classification performance even with aggressive compression, while LPC shows slightly larger degradation.
conclusion: Substantial dimensionality reduction is possible with minimal accuracy loss, enabling lightweight cybersecurity analytics.

title: Explainable AI-Driven Cyber Risk Analytics And Model Reliability Assessment For Intelligent Governance Of U.s. Critical Infrastructure: An XGBoost And SHAP-Based Intrusion Detection Framework
authors: B. M. Taslimul Haque, Md. Arifur Rahman, Md. Serajul Kabir Chowdhury Rubel, Md. Iqbal Hossan
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05710v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The increasing penetrations of the critical infrastructure sector in the United States with intelligent digital technologies have greatly increased exposure to advanced cyber adversaries and operational vulnerabilities. AI-powered governance and automated decision-making systems are becoming a key part of the operation of critical infrastructure systems, including energy, healthcare, transportation, financial services, and communication infrastructure, in order to improve efficiency and strategic management. The growing cyber threat environment, such as Distributed Denial of Service (DDos) attacks, botnets, ransomware, and Advanced Persistent Threats (APTs) pose significant challenges to infrastructure resilience, cyber security reliability, and governance trustworthiness. In a changing attack landscape and dynamic network environment, traditional cybersecurity mechanisms can often fall short of meeting the evolving needs and protecting critical systems. This study will develop a resilient cyber risk analytics and model reliability assessment framework to support intelligent governance and decision support for cyber risk exposure in the U.S. critical infrastructure environment. This study is based on the CICIDS2017 dataset for the development and testing of intrusion detection system models and cyber risk prediction models based on machine learning. Various classifiers like XGBoost, Random Forest, and Decision Tree are used to detect malicious activities on the network and determine the level of cyber risk. Furthermore, the Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) techniques are integrated to enhance transparency, interpretability, and trust in cybersecurity decision-making processes. The proposed framework presents the reliability and resilience of the model by having various performance measures such as accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score, ROC-AUC, and false positive rate.
tldr: This paper applies XGBoost and SHAP for intrusion detection in U.S. critical infrastructure, focusing on cyber risk analytics and model reliability.
motivation: To address the growing cyber threats to critical infrastructure and the limitations of traditional cybersecurity mechanisms.
method: Uses the CICIDS2017 dataset and machine learning classifiers (XGBoost, Random Forest, Decision Tree) with Explainable AI (SHAP) for intrusion detection and risk prediction.
result: The proposed framework demonstrates high performance metrics (accuracy, precision, recall, F1, ROC-AUC) and enhanced interpretability via SHAP.
conclusion: The framework supports intelligent governance and decision-making for cybersecurity, but further validation on real-world data is needed.

title: An Improved Cnn-lstm Based Intrusion Detection System For IoT Networks
authors: Mohammad Tariq Ikhlas, Pohanyar Khowaja Khil, Malik Muhammad Mueed Aslam, Muhammad Khuram Shahzad
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05776v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: With the rapid proliferation of IoT devices, security concerns have dramatically escalated and intrusion detection systems have become critical for protecting networked environments. This paper presents an improved CNN-LSTM based intrusion detection model that combines multi-class classification, dataset integration, and temporal feature learning to enhance detection performance in IoT networks. Using network traffic data, the proposed approach is evaluated on intrusion detection tasks and achieves an accuracy of approximately 97%. Experimental results demonstrate that the model effectively detects multiple attack categories while maintaining stable training and validation performance. The integration of convolutional and recurrent neural network components enables the framework to capture both spatial and temporal characteristics of network traffic, improving overall intrusion detection capability in IoT environments.
tldr: This paper proposes a CNN-LSTM based intrusion detection system for IoT networks, achieving 97% accuracy on network traffic data.
motivation: To address security concerns in IoT networks by improving intrusion detection performance.
method: Combines convolutional and recurrent neural network components to capture spatial and temporal features of network traffic, using multi-class classification and dataset integration.
result: The model achieves approximately 97% accuracy in detecting multiple attack categories with stable training and validation performance.
conclusion: The proposed CNN-LSTM framework enhances intrusion detection capability in IoT environments, but the paper does not discuss energy consumption or quantum aspects.

title: TinyML-Driven Cybersecurity For Autonomous Spacecraft: Latency-Accuracy Analysis For Sparta Rf And Cyber Threat Detection
authors: van Le, Trevor Tran, Tan Le
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05779v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Autonomous spacecraft require rapid, lightweight, and reliable onboard detection of cyber-RF threats. Using the SPARTA attack model, we analyze the latency-accuracy trade-offs of TinyML-compatible classical models -- Random Forest, Logistic Regression, SVM, and MLP -- for detecting uplink jamming, Fake-NR spoofing, payload manipulation, ground-segment compromise, and unauthorized command injection. We present a physics-informed theoretical analysis of each model's computational complexity, VC dimension, Lipschitz continuity, and latency scaling, supported by empirical measurements on adversarial RF spectrograms generated via BandErasure, FakeNR, and NoiseBurst corruption modes. Results show that Logistic Regression achieves microsecond-level inference with only a 1\% accuracy drop relative to Random Forest, making it an effective TinyML baseline for onboard autonomy. The study also identifies opportunities for advancing spacecraft cybersecurity through richer feature encoders and multi-timescale learning architectures, building on recent progress in edge intelligence and trustworthy AI.
tldr: This paper evaluates TinyML models for cyber-RF threat detection in autonomous spacecraft, focusing on latency-accuracy trade-offs.
motivation: Autonomous spacecraft need lightweight onboard detection of cyber-RF threats, but existing models may be too heavy or slow.
method: The authors analyze Random Forest, Logistic Regression, SVM, and MLP using physics-informed theoretical analysis (complexity, VC dimension, Lipschitz continuity) and empirical tests on adversarial RF spectrograms.
result: Logistic Regression achieves microsecond inference with only 1% accuracy drop compared to Random Forest, making it a suitable TinyML baseline.
conclusion: The study suggests opportunities for richer feature encoders and multi-timescale learning architectures for spacecraft cybersecurity.

title: SentinelRAG: Synthetic Sentinel Knowledge For Rag Database Copyright Protection
authors: Tsun On Kwok, Xi Yang, Ki Sen Hung, Chang Liu, Yangqiu Song
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05787v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Protecting proprietary RAG databases from unauthorized redistribution is challenging: existing watermarking methods either inject fabricated relations between real entities, polluting the knowledge base with misinformation, or embed fragile lexical patterns that adversarial paraphrasing easily removes. We propose SentinelRAG, a watermarking framework that embeds style-consistent but fictitious knowledge entries into the RAG database. Our key insight is that synthetic knowledge describing fictitious entities is unlikely to be retrieved by legitimate queries, yet can be reliably triggered through targeted probes known only to the data owner. Experiments on four datasets ranging from 2.9k to 8.8M documents demonstrate that SentinelRAG achieves statistically significant detection [MATH] across all tested configurations at only a 0.1% injection rate. Compared to the state-of-the-art, our method significantly reduces the false detection rate while maintaining negligible interference with legitimate user queries.
tldr: SentinelRAG embeds fictitious knowledge entries into RAG databases for copyright protection, with minimal impact on legitimate queries.
motivation: Existing watermarking methods for RAG databases either introduce misinformation or are vulnerable to adversarial paraphrasing.
method: The framework injects style-consistent but fictitious knowledge entries that are unlikely to be retrieved by legitimate queries but can be triggered by targeted probes.
result: Experiments on four datasets show statistically significant detection at only 0.1% injection rate, with reduced false detection rate compared to state-of-the-art.
conclusion: SentinelRAG offers a robust watermarking approach for RAG database copyright protection with negligible interference to legitimate users.

title: Towards Worst-case Hardness For Low-Noise Lpn
authors: Divesh Aggarwal, Rishav Gupta, Hai Hoang Nguyen, Kel Zin Tan, Prashant Nalini Vasudevan
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05834v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The hardness of the Learning Parity with Noise (LPN) problem is a foundational assumption in cryptography, forming the basis of constructions ranging from symmetric-key primitives to public-key encryption and beyond. A central open question is whether the average-case hardness of LPN can be based on worst-case complexity assumptions, as has been achieved for the analogous Learning With Errors (LWE) problem. Existing worst-case-to-average-case reductions for LPN [BLVW19, YZ21] rely on statistical smoothing of linear codes, which inherently limits the resulting average-case hardness to noise rates as large as [MATH], which is insufficient for public-key applications. We explore a new approach towards obtaining such reductions: rather than requiring that random sparse combinations of the rows of the generator matrix of a code be statistically close to uniform, we only require that they be computationally indistinguishable from uniform. This leads to a clean win-win structure: we show that any efficient LPN solver can be transformed into a pair of efficient algorithms [MATH] such that for every matrix [MATH] of appropriate dimensions over [MATH], either [MATH] decodes the code generated by [MATH] from random noise, or [MATH] distinguishes random noisy codewords of the dual of this code from uniform. By instantiating this reduction with appropriate parameters, we obtain the average-case hardness of LPN with inverse-polynomial noise rate [MATH] for any constant [MATH], assuming the worst-case simultaneous hardness of decoding a code from random noise and distinguishing random noisy codewords of its dual from uniform. In particular, setting [MATH], our reduction yields LPN hardness in the parameter regime required for Alekhnovich's construction of public-key encryption [Ale03], a regime that was previously inaccessible via worst-case reductions.
tldr: This paper proposes a new approach to prove worst-case hardness for the Learning Parity with Noise (LPN) problem, aiming to enable public-key encryption from worst-case assumptions.
motivation: Existing worst-case-to-average-case reductions for LPN only work for high noise rates, insufficient for public-key applications. The authors aim to achieve reductions for low-noise LPN.
method: Instead of requiring statistical smoothing of linear codes, they only require computational indistinguishability, leading to a win-win reduction that transforms any LPN solver into either a decoder or a distinguisher.
result: They obtain average-case hardness of LPN with inverse-polynomial noise rate under worst-case simultaneous hardness of decoding and distinguishing dual codewords.
conclusion: This reduction yields LPN hardness in the parameter regime needed for Alekhnovich's public-key encryption, previously inaccessible via worst-case reductions.

title: GenTI: Benchmarking LLMs For Autonomous Idps Rule Generation For Unseen Attacks
authors: Hassan Jalil Hadi, Rehana Yasmin, Ali Shoker
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05844v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Rule-based Intrusion Detection and Prevention Systems (IDPS) offer precise attack detection as well as mitigation, however their manually crafted, signature-driven rules limit adaptability to emerging and zero-day threats. Additionally, existing public datasets (e.g., CICIDS2017, UNSW-NB15) focus on traffic classification and provide little structured information to support automatic rule synthesis or prevention logic. To address this gap, we propose Generative Thread Intelligence (GenTI) an LLM-driven benchmark for automatic generation of IDPS rules targeting unseen attacks. The dataset (GTI) aggregates over 150k detection and prevention rules from Snort, Suricata, Emerging Threats, as well as 50k YARA, each annotated with protocol behavior, payload signatures, contextual relationships, mappings to Cyber Threat Intelligence (CTI), along with actionable response types (alert, drop, reject). Moreover, on top of this corpus we design an LLM-based pipeline that transforms analyst prompts and representative payloads into deployable rules via structured prompt engineering, Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning, as well as a Chain-of-Verification (CoVe) loop for syntactic, semantic, and security validation. The generated rules are executed in real time on (Snort/Suricata) and evaluated by syntax accuracy, semantic similarity, CTI coverage, security effectiveness as well as unseen attacks detection. Furthermore, our GenTI instantiation achieves a composite rule-quality score of 89.4\%, with 94.8\% CTI coverage, improving unseen attacks detection from 45\% to 87.4\% and reducing the false-positive rate from 8.5\% to 2.3\%. Overall, GenTI establishes the first large-scale benchmark that tightly couples rule-level CTI with LLM-based automation, enabling adaptive, self-evolving IDPS.
tldr: This paper introduces GenTI, a benchmark and LLM-based pipeline for automatically generating IDPS rules to detect unseen attacks.
motivation: Existing rule-based IDPS systems rely on manually crafted signatures that fail against emerging and zero-day threats, and current datasets lack structured information for automatic rule synthesis.
method: The authors aggregate over 200k detection/prevention rules from Snort, Suricata, Emerging Threats, and YARA, annotate them with protocol behavior, payload signatures, and CTI mappings, then design an LLM pipeline using prompt engineering, Chain-of-Thought reasoning, and Chain-of-Verification to generate deployable rules.
result: GenTI achieves a composite rule-quality score of 89.4%, 94.8% CTI coverage, improves unseen attack detection from 45% to 87.4%, and reduces false-positive rate from 8.5% to 2.3%.
conclusion: GenTI provides a large-scale benchmark coupling rule-level CTI with LLM automation, enabling adaptive, self-evolving IDPS systems.

title: Exploring Cooperation Mechanisms Via Reinforcement Learning In Network Common-pool Resource Games
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05867v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sustaining cooperation in resource-constrained populations requires allocation mechanisms that balance individual incentives, resource sustainability, and distributional fairness. This paper proposes a network common-pool resource game in which individuals are embedded in complex networks, participate in multiple overlapping local resource pools, and face endogenous resource constraints during strategy evolution. Within this framework, we first examine two representative allocation mechanisms, equal allocation and proportional allocation. The results show that equal allocation produces fair but inefficient outcomes by weakening contribution incentives, whereas proportional allocation can temporarily promote cooperation but amplifies accumulated advantages and leads to severe inequality. To overcome these limitations, we develop a graph neural network-based reinforcement learning framework in which a learned social planner allocates local pool resources without directly controlling individual strategies. Simulation results under four representative network topologies show that the learned planner sustains higher cooperation levels and average accumulated resources, and reduces inequality compared with the baselines. Furthermore, we interpret the learned policy and distill it into two simpler mechanisms: a resource-dependent mixture mechanism for regular networks and a degree-conditioned mixture mechanism for heterogeneous networks. These mechanisms reveal that effective allocation should adapt to both local resource states and structural positions, providing an interpretable route from reinforcement learning policy search to mechanism design in networked resource-sharing systems.
tldr: This paper uses reinforcement learning to design allocation mechanisms for sustaining cooperation in networked common-pool resource games, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To overcome limitations of equal and proportional allocation mechanisms in sustaining cooperation and reducing inequality in networked resource-sharing systems.
method: A graph neural network-based reinforcement learning framework trains a social planner to allocate local pool resources without controlling individual strategies, tested on four network topologies.
result: The learned planner sustains higher cooperation, higher average resources, and reduces inequality compared to baselines; the policy is distilled into simpler mechanisms adapted to resource states and structural positions.
conclusion: Effective allocation should adapt to local resource states and structural positions, providing an interpretable route from RL policy search to mechanism design in networked resource-sharing systems.

title: Metric Facility Assignment With Partial Information
authors: Vasilis Gkatzelis, Hasti Karimi, Emma Rewinski, Maziar Shamsipour, Alexandros A. Voudouris
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05905v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study an assignment problem where a set of agents and a set of facilities lie on a line metric. The goal is to compute an assignment of agents to facilities to approximately minimize the social cost (the total distance of agents from their assigned facilities) given only partial information regarding the metric. Unlike previous work which focused solely on algorithms with access to the ordinal preferences of the agents over the facilities (ORD), we also consider the value of information regarding approval preferences (APP), and inter-facility distances (DIST). For different combinations of these three information types, we establish tight bounds on the distortion of deterministic algorithms, showing that it is possible to improve over the optimal bound of [MATH] that can be achieved using only ORD information. Among other results, we show a tight bound of [MATH] for APP+DIST which holds even for general metrics, and a tight bound of [MATH] for ORD+APP+DIST.
tldr: This paper studies the metric facility assignment problem with partial information, focusing on distortion bounds for different information types.
motivation: To understand how different types of partial information (ordinal preferences, approval preferences, inter-facility distances) can improve the quality of facility assignment algorithms.
method: The authors consider deterministic algorithms with access to combinations of ORD, APP, and DIST information, and derive tight distortion bounds.
result: They establish tight bounds on distortion for various information combinations, showing improvements over using only ordinal preferences.
conclusion: The results provide a complete picture of the power of different partial information types in metric facility assignment.

title: The Complexity Of Asynchronous HyperLTL
abstract: ArXiv:2606.06091v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hyperproperties express, e.g., information-flow properties of systems, which involves the simultaneous reasoning about multiple execution traces of a system. Consequently, HyperLTL, the most important specification logic for hyperproperties, extends LTL with quantification over traces. However, HyperLTL can only express synchronous hyperproperties. Recently, several logics for asynchronous hyperproperties have been proposed. Here, we focus on AHLTL, asynchronous HyperLTL, which extends HyperLTL with quantification over trajectories that control the relative speed at which time progresses on the quantified traces. Model-checking AHLTL is known to be undecidable while satisfiability is known to be [MATH]-hard, but the precise complexity of both problems is open. Here, we close these gaps and show that model-checking is equivalent to truth in second-order arithmetic while satisfiability is [MATH]-complete if the trajectory is existentially quantified and [MATH]-hard and in [MATH] if the trajectory is universally quantified.
tldr: This paper settles the complexity of model-checking and satisfiability for asynchronous HyperLTL, showing model-checking is equivalent to truth in second-order arithmetic and satisfiability is Σ1^1-complete or Π1^1-hard/in Π1^1 depending on quantifier type.
motivation: HyperLTL can only express synchronous hyperproperties, but many real-world systems require asynchronous reasoning. The precise complexity of AHLTL (asynchronous HyperLTL) was unknown, hindering its practical use.
method: The authors use reductions from second-order arithmetic and known complexity classes to prove completeness and hardness results for AHLTL model-checking and satisfiability.
result: Model-checking AHLTL is equivalent to truth in second-order arithmetic (highly undecidable), while satisfiability is Σ1^1-complete for existential trajectory quantification and Π1^1-hard/in Π1^1 for universal trajectory quantification.
conclusion: AHLTL is extremely expressive but computationally intractable, suggesting that practical verification of asynchronous hyperproperties may require restrictions or alternative logics.

title: Regret Minimization In Single-Dimensional Contract-Design With Binary Actions
authors: Riccardo Poiani, Martino Bernasconi, Andrea Celli
abstract: ArXiv:2606.06125v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study principal-agent problems in which a principal commits to an outcome-dependent payment scheme (i.e., a contract) in order to induce an agent to take a costly action leading to a favorable outcome. We consider the online extension of the classical (one-shot) principal-agent problem, in which the principal repeatedly interacts with agents by proposing contracts over multiple rounds. The principal has no information about the agents and, crucially, does not observe their actions. As a result, the principal must learn an optimal contract using only the realized outcomes observed at each round. We focus on the setting with binary actions and single-dimensional agent types, where the agent's private type represents their cost per unit-of-effort. For adversarial-type sequences, we provide tight [MATH] regret guarantees. Remarkably, this rate is completely independent of the number of outcomes [MATH]. The upper bound is based on two key components: 1) a reduction to a one-dimensional threshold optimization problem and 2) a non-uniform discretization to handle the non-Lipschitz nature of the problem. Moreover, in the case of a single (fixed) hidden type, we show that it is possible to improve the rates and provide a tight [MATH] regret bound. Our algorithm is based on an explore-then-commit strategy where we first approximately learn the hidden type via a stochastic binary search, and then we commit to a ``robustified'' near-optimal contract.
tldr: This paper studies online contract design with binary actions and single-dimensional agent types, providing regret bounds for principal-agent problems.
motivation: To understand how a principal can learn optimal contracts over multiple rounds without observing agent actions, in adversarial and stochastic settings.
method: Reduces the problem to one-dimensional threshold optimization and uses non-uniform discretization; for fixed hidden type, employs explore-then-commit with stochastic binary search.
result: Achieves tight regret bounds independent of the number of outcomes for adversarial types, and improved bounds for a single fixed type.
conclusion: Provides foundational results for online contract design, with implications for algorithmic mechanism design and learning in principal-agent settings.

title: Decoupling Adhesion From Jamming In Phase Transitions Drives Tissue Organization
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 02 June 2026;
tldr: This paper studies how adhesion and cell density control phase transitions in cellular collectives, driving tissue organization.
motivation: To understand how multiple control parameters, specifically cell density and adhesion, regulate phase transitions in tissues and influence developmental programs.
method: Combined in silico modeling and in vivo experiments to independently tune cell density and adhesion, observing their effects on tissue material state and organization.
result: Adhesion dictates the tissue material state; adhesion-driven solidification in unjammed pluripotent tissues drives epithelial organization, showing that phase transitions direct developmental programs.
conclusion: The findings reveal a mechanism where adhesion controls tissue solidification, providing insights into how physical principles govern biological development.

title: Thorium-229 Lifetime Locked Down
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 29 May 2026;
tldr: The paper resolves a decade-long puzzle about the anomalously short lifetime of a nuclear metastable state in thorium-229 ions, revealing an uncommon decay channel.
motivation: The lifetime of the nuclear metastable state in singly charged thorium-229 ions appeared shorter than theoretical predictions, motivating a search for the underlying decay mechanism.
method: Experimental measurements and theoretical analysis were combined to investigate the decay of the metastable state in thorium-229 ions.
result: The discrepancy was resolved by identifying an uncommon decay channel that accounts for the shorter lifetime.
conclusion: The findings provide a deeper understanding of nuclear decay processes and may impact applications in nuclear clocks and fundamental physics.

title: Universal Deformations And Universal Residual Stresses In Incompressible Isotropic Cauchy Elasticity
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05416v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study universal deformations in incompressible isotropic Cauchy elastic solids with residual stress, without assuming any specific origin for the residual stress. Starting from the constitutive representation of the Cauchy stress as an isotropic tensor-valued function of strain and residual stress, we derive the universality constraints for residually-stressed incompressible isotropic Cauchy elastic solids. We show that for the six known families of universal deformations the set of universal deformations is identical to that of incompressible isotropic elasticity in the absence of residual stress. We also show that residual stress does not enlarge the space of universal deformations. We then determine the universal residual stress fields corresponding to the six known families of universal deformations. Assuming that the residual stress field has the same symmetry as the corresponding universal deformation, the universality constraints reduce to systems of ordinary differential equations that can be solved explicitly. The resulting universal residual stress fields are characterized and discussed for each family.
tldr: This paper studies universal deformations and residual stresses in incompressible isotropic Cauchy elastic solids, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand how residual stress affects universal deformations in nonlinear elasticity, without assuming a specific origin for the stress.
method: Derives universality constraints from constitutive representation of Cauchy stress as isotropic function of strain and residual stress, then solves ODEs for symmetric residual stress fields.
result: The six known families of universal deformations remain unchanged; residual stress does not enlarge the space. Explicit universal residual stress fields are characterized for each family.
conclusion: Provides a complete classification of universal residual stress fields in incompressible isotropic Cauchy elasticity, with implications for experimental design and material modeling.

title: Introduction To Measure And Integration Theory
authors: Hugo Guadalupe Reyna-Casta\~neda, Mar\'ia de Los \'angeles Sandoval-Romero, Luis Antonio Cede\~no-P\'erez
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05215v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: These notes provide a rigorous and accessible introduction to measure and integration theory, with emphasis on the conceptual transition from the Riemann integral to the Lebesgue integral and the role played by limiting processes in modern analysis. The manuscript develops the basic theory of measurable sets, measurable functions, measures on [MATH]-algebras, Lebesgue integration, convergence theorems, and [MATH] spaces. Particular attention is devoted to the interaction between integration and convergence, as well as to the limitations of the Riemann integral that motivate the development of measure theory. The exposition seeks to balance mathematical rigor with pedagogical clarity through detailed proofs, examples, exercises, and supplementary projects. These notes are intended primarily for undergraduate students in mathematics and related areas encountering measure theory for the first time, although they may also serve as a reference for introductory graduate courses in analysis.
tldr: This paper is a pedagogical introduction to measure and integration theory, covering Lebesgue integration and convergence theorems.
motivation: To provide a rigorous yet accessible introduction to measure theory for undergraduate students, highlighting the limitations of the Riemann integral.
method: Expository text with detailed proofs, examples, exercises, and supplementary projects.
result: Develops basic theory of measurable sets, functions, measures, Lebesgue integration, convergence theorems, and Lp spaces.
conclusion: Serves as a textbook for students new to measure theory; no novel research contributions.

title: Some Properties Of Besov-Morrey Type Spaces
authors: A. Ussentay, K. Sadykova, N. Tleukhanova
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05432v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper considers Sobolev-Morrey and Besov-Morrey spaces. For Morrey spaces, multipliers are studied, and a theorem on multipliers from M_p^lambda(T) to M_p^lambda(T) is obtained for 1 < p < infinity and 0 <= lambda < 1/p. Based on this result, embeddings between Besov-Morrey and Sobolev-type spaces are established, namely B_1^alpha(M_p^lambda) embedded into W^alpha(M_p^lambda) embedded into B_infinity^alpha(M_p^lambda) for 0 < p <= infinity, 0 <= lambda <= 1/p, and alpha in R. In addition, an interpolation theorem for Besov-Morrey spaces is proved.
tldr: This paper studies function spaces (Sobolev-Morrey and Besov-Morrey) and their embeddings, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand multipliers and embeddings for Morrey-type spaces, which are of interest in harmonic analysis.
method: Analytical proofs using functional analysis and interpolation theory.
result: Established embeddings between Besov-Morrey and Sobolev-type spaces, and an interpolation theorem for Besov-Morrey spaces.
conclusion: The results contribute to the theory of function spaces but have no direct application to the user's research areas.

title: Weighted hp-Uniform Decompositions For H^k-Type Tensor-Product Spaces In Arbitrary Dimension
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05615v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish weighted hp-uniform vertex-patch decompositions in arbitrary space dimension d >= 1 for tensor-product discretizations of H^k-type conforming and nonconforming spaces, with arbitrary fixed Sobolev order k >= 1, on fitted interface meshes. The cells are coordinate-compatible cuboids, the local spaces are Q_{p_K}(K) with arbitrary elementwise degrees satisfying p_K >= 2k-1, and the coefficient may have arbitrarily large jumps across material interfaces. Under local coefficient oscillation bounds and a local high-side connectivity condition, both the conforming H^k space and the nonconforming spaces V_h^{(s)}, 0 <= s <= k, admit stable decompositions with constants which may depend on the fixed parameters d and k, but are independent of the mesh size, all polynomial degrees, neighboring degree ratios, and the global coefficient contrast. The argument combines a Hermite endpoint transform for endpoint jets of order 0,...,k-1, its tensor-product extension, weighted broken patch Poincare inequalities, and a successive correction of normal derivative jumps. Numerical experiments for a three-dimensional DG problem with large coefficient jumps and strongly varying local polynomial degrees support the predicted robustness. For k = 1 the same conclusions hold on uniformly regular mapped cubical meshes whose neighboring element maps agree on each common face.
tldr: This paper develops weighted hp-uniform decompositions for tensor-product finite element spaces on interface meshes, focusing on numerical analysis and robustness for high-order discretizations.
motivation: To establish stable decompositions for H^k-type conforming and nonconforming spaces on fitted interface meshes with large coefficient jumps and varying polynomial degrees, which is important for numerical methods like DG.
method: Combines Hermite endpoint transform, tensor-product extension, weighted broken patch Poincaré inequalities, and successive correction of normal derivative jumps.
result: Proved stable decompositions with constants independent of mesh size, polynomial degrees, degree ratios, and coefficient contrast, supported by 3D DG experiments.
conclusion: The results provide robust theoretical foundations for hp-adaptive methods on complex geometries, but are purely numerical analysis with no direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: On Parallel And Batch-Cutting Strategies For Norm-Minimization-Based Convex Vector Optimization
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05617v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop parallel and batch-cutting variants of the norm-minimization-based outer approximation algorithm for convex vector optimization. The standard algorithm solves [MATH] independent subproblems at each iteration~[MATH] to evaluate all vertices of the current polyhedral approximation, but processes only the single best cut. We propose two improvements. First, we parallelize the across [MATH] workers, reducing per-iteration wall-clock time. Second, we introduce a batch-cutting strategy that adds up to [MATH] supporting halfspaces per iteration, using information from all solved subproblems rather than discarding it. We prove that the batch-cutting variant inherits the convergence rate [MATH] of the standard algorithm, where [MATH] is the number of outer iterations and [MATH] is the number of objectives. Computational experiments on eight test problems with [MATH] show that parallelism on 8 cores , and batch cutting consistently reduces the iteration count by 62--80\%. However, the wall-clock benefit of batch cutting is problem-dependent: the additional cuts per iteration accelerate vertex count growth, so batch cutting is most effective when per-vertex subproblem cost dominates.
tldr: This paper proposes parallel and batch-cutting strategies for a norm-minimization-based convex vector optimization algorithm, improving computational efficiency.
motivation: To reduce the wall-clock time and iteration count of the standard norm-minimization-based outer approximation algorithm for convex vector optimization.
method: The authors parallelize the evaluation of subproblems across multiple workers and introduce a batch-cutting strategy that adds multiple supporting halfspaces per iteration using information from all solved subproblems.
result: Parallelism on 8 cores and batch cutting reduce iteration count by 62-80%, but wall-clock benefit of batch cutting depends on per-vertex subproblem cost.
conclusion: The batch-cutting variant inherits the convergence rate of the standard algorithm, and its effectiveness is problem-dependent; future work may explore further optimizations.

title: Trace-Class Results For Mcmc Algorithms For Student-t Regression Models
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05672v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we consider MCMC algorithms for Student-[MATH] regression models. We investigate the efficiency of Markov chains based on the algorithms in terms of whether trace-class results hold or not. We first consider the case where the regression coefficients and error variance follow the invariant improper prior distributions. The Markov operator associated with a standard data augmentation algorithm is not trace-class but that associated with a collpased Gibbs algorithm is trace-class. We next consider the case where the parameters follow a normal-inverse gamma distribution. In this case, the standard Markov operator is trace-class.
tldr: This paper analyzes trace-class properties of MCMC algorithms for Student-t regression models, which is unrelated to the user's research interests in quantum information and thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand the efficiency of MCMC algorithms for Bayesian Student-t regression, specifically whether the Markov operators are trace-class.
method: Theoretical analysis of Markov operators for standard data augmentation and collapsed Gibbs algorithms under different prior distributions.
result: The collapsed Gibbs algorithm yields a trace-class operator under improper priors, while the standard algorithm does not; under normal-inverse gamma priors, the standard operator is trace-class.
conclusion: The findings provide guidance on choosing efficient MCMC algorithms for Student-t regression, but have no connection to quantum computing or information thermodynamics.

title: Derivations Of Rational Vertex Operator Algebras Are Inner
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05854v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that every derivation of a simple and rational vertex operator algebra of CFT type is an inner derivation.
tldr: This paper proves that all derivations of simple rational vertex operator algebras of CFT type are inner derivations.
motivation: To understand the structure of derivations in vertex operator algebras, which is important for the algebraic theory of conformal field theory.
method: The paper uses algebraic methods within the theory of vertex operator algebras, likely involving cohomology or representation theory.
result: Every derivation of a simple rational vertex operator algebra of CFT type is inner.
conclusion: This result clarifies the derivation algebra of such VOAs, which may have implications for the classification of VOAs and their modules.

title: On Strong Identities Of Almost-canonically Seminormed Rings
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05965v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the strong identity condition (SIC) for almost-canonically seminormed rings, a class of topological graded rings that includes enveloping algebras of vertex operator algebras. This condition was introduced in the algebro-geometric theory of conformal blocks, where it governs the smoothing of nodal curves. To understand the representation-theoretic meaning of SIC, we develop the representation theory of almost-canonically seminormed rings, including Zhu-type algebras, induced modules, rationality conditions, tensor product compatibility, and an end formula for the mode transition algebra. Our main result characterizes the strong identity condition in terms of orthogonal expansions, projectivity of canonical modules, and Morita-type equivalences induced by Zhu-type algebras. As an application, we show that for vertex operator algebras of CFT type, the smoothing property is equivalent to the Zhu algebra inducing a Morita-type equivalence with the category of admissible modules. Consequently, the strong identity condition identifies the precise representation-theoretic obstruction to extending algebraic smoothing beyond the semisimple setting. We further illustrate the theory through explicit examples, including the Weyl algebra and several irrational vertex operator algebras where the strong identity condition fails.
tldr: This paper studies strong identities in almost-canonically seminormed rings, a purely algebraic topic with no connection to quantum information or condensed matter physics.
motivation: To understand the representation-theoretic meaning of the strong identity condition (SIC) in the algebro-geometric theory of conformal blocks.
method: Develops representation theory of almost-canonically seminormed rings, including Zhu-type algebras, induced modules, and Morita-type equivalences.
result: Characterizes SIC in terms of orthogonal expansions and projectivity; shows that for vertex operator algebras of CFT type, smoothing property is equivalent to a Morita-type equivalence.
conclusion: Identifies representation-theoretic obstruction to extending algebraic smoothing beyond semisimple settings; provides examples where SIC fails.

title: Bitcoin After Block Rewards
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05503v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Bitcoin's block reward is scheduled to decline to zero, raising concerns about whether the network can remain secure once miners rely solely on transaction fees. This paper seeks to identify the conditions under which large-scale and persistent deviation from honest mining can arise. We analyze and compare the payoffs of honest and deviating miners in a sequential decision model, and identify a deviation threshold [MATH] at which honest mining ceases to be privately optimal. Around the 2024 Bitcoin halving, we show that current mining behavior does not exhibit large-scale or structural deviation. However, when the block reward is removed, the [MATH] criterion implies that deviation can arise even with a very small fraction of transaction fees. Finally, we evaluate three protocol-level mechanisms: Base Fee, Fee Floor, and an adaptive maximum block size rule, and show that their combination raises the deviation threshold and mitigates incentive breakdown in a fee-only regime. These results provide a practical benchmark for assessing Bitcoin's security as block rewards disappear.
tldr: This paper analyzes Bitcoin's security after block rewards end, focusing on miner incentives and protocol mechanisms to prevent deviation.
motivation: Bitcoin's block reward will eventually disappear, raising concerns about network security when miners rely solely on transaction fees.
method: The authors use a sequential decision model to compare payoffs of honest and deviating miners, and evaluate three protocol-level mechanisms.
result: A deviation threshold is identified; around the 2024 halving no large-scale deviation is observed, but after block rewards end, deviation can arise even with small transaction fees. Combining Base Fee, Fee Floor, and adaptive max block size raises the threshold.
conclusion: The proposed mechanisms can mitigate incentive breakdown in a fee-only regime, providing a benchmark for Bitcoin's security as block rewards disappear.

title: Cognitive Threat Intelligence And Explainable Federated Security Analytics For Distributed Infrastructure Systems
authors: Md. Arifur Rahman, B. M. Taslimul Haque, Md. Iqbal Hossan, Md. Serajul Kabir Chowdhury Rubel
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05701v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The increasing adoption of distributed infrastructure systems, cloud computing, Internet of Things (IoT) technologies, and edge-based architectures has significantly expanded the cybersecurity attack surface and introduced increasingly sophisticated cyber threats. Conventional centralized intrusion detection approaches often face challenges related to scalability, data privacy, communication overhead, and limited transparency in artificial intelligence-driven decision-making processes. To address these limitations, this study proposes a Cognitive Threat Intelligence and Explainable Federated Security Analytics framework for distributed infrastructure systems. The proposed framework integrates Federated Learning (FL), Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI), and cognitive cybersecurity analytics to enable collaborative and privacy-preserving cyber threat detection across distributed network environments. Instead of transmitting sensitive raw network traffic data to centralized servers, local security models are independently trained at distributed nodes, where only encrypted model parameters and updates are shared through a federated aggregation mechanism. This decentralized learning architecture improves privacy protection while reducing communication dependency and centralized security risks. To enhance intelligent threat analysis, the framework incorporates machine learning and deep learning algorithms including Random Forest, XGBoost, Autoencoder.
tldr: This paper proposes a federated learning framework with explainable AI for cybersecurity threat detection in distributed infrastructure, but it is unrelated to quantum computing or the user's research interests.
motivation: Conventional centralized intrusion detection faces scalability, privacy, and transparency issues in distributed systems.
method: Integrates Federated Learning, Explainable AI, and cognitive analytics; local models are trained on distributed nodes and only encrypted parameters are shared.
result: The framework enables privacy-preserving collaborative threat detection with reduced communication overhead.
conclusion: The approach improves security analytics but is not connected to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: An Embarrassingly Simple Detector For Model Extraction Attacks In Large Language Model Api Traffic
authors: Shuze Liu, Qianwen Guo, Yushun Dong
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05725v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed through hosted APIs, making model extraction a practical threat to model ownership and service security. However, individual extraction queries often resemble benign requests, and existing evaluations often focus on single-query anomaly scoring or pure benign-versus-attacker user settings. We formulate model extraction monitoring as benign-calibrated traffic-window distribution testing and show that an embarrassingly simple detector is effective: embed incoming queries into a semantic space and test whether their aggregate distribution deviates from historical benign traffic. We instantiate the detector with maximum mean discrepancy (MMD), using only benign-vs-benign comparisons to set the decision threshold. We evaluate on fourteen attacker-normal query pairs from four extraction scenarios and compare with adapted PRADA, SEAT, CAP, DATE, and marginal Mahalanobis baselines. Across three random seeds, MMD achieves 0.3% benign FPR, 100.0% pure-attacker TPR, 90.5% average TPR over attacker fractions, and 95.1% balanced accuracy. These results show that benign-calibrated distribution testing is a strong empirical baseline for model extraction detection in both user-level and mixed multi-user LLM API traffic. Code is released at: [URL].
tldr: This paper proposes a simple detector for model extraction attacks on LLM APIs using distribution testing with MMD, achieving high detection rates.
motivation: Model extraction attacks pose a threat to LLM service security, but existing detection methods are complex or evaluated in unrealistic settings.
method: The detector embeds queries into a semantic space and uses maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) to compare the distribution of incoming traffic against historical benign traffic, with thresholds set using benign-vs-benign comparisons.
result: The MMD-based detector achieves 0.3% benign FPR, 100% pure-attacker TPR, 90.5% average TPR over attacker fractions, and 95.1% balanced accuracy across 14 attack scenarios.
conclusion: Benign-calibrated distribution testing is a strong baseline for model extraction detection in LLM API traffic, and the method is simple yet effective.

title: Exploring The Connection Between Coding Habits And Cognitive Styles In Malware Developers
authors: Vasilis Vouvoutsis, Constantinos Patsakis, Fran Casino
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05945v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Malware research primarily studies the results, the methods, and the impact. Even from an offensive security perspective, what is examined is the method, not the development strategy of the offender. This study investigates the behavioral signatures and coding patterns embedded in the malware source code. By analyzing a large corpus of leaked malware code and comparing it with carefully selected benign open-source software, we apply static application security testing and compute multiple software metrics. Based on cognitive psychology and criminological theories, our work interprets differences in code structure and quality as behavioral indicators, reflecting distinct motivational structures, risk tolerances, and development strategies of malware authors compared to benign software developers. Our findings reveal that malware code is generally smaller, less documented, and exhibits higher cyclomatic complexity per function, with reduced use of abstraction mechanisms such as classes and closures. Vulnerability analysis further reveals that malware exhibits more issues of the types that benign code typically avoids, suggesting a minimal investment in secure development practices. These patterns imply a development style optimized for expedience, operational secrecy, and evasion rather than long-term maintainability. Nonetheless, the code quality metrics indicate that it does not deviate significantly from benign software enough to be distinctive. By framing code metrics as proxies for behavioral signals and strategic choices, we demonstrate how quantitative software analysis can enrich behavioral cybersecurity research, offering new insights into the practices and priorities of malware developers. Our results pave the way for further research in the behavioral profiling of cyber offenders.
tldr: This paper analyzes coding patterns in malware source code to infer behavioral traits of malware developers, but it is unrelated to quantum computing, condensed matter physics, or machine learning.
motivation: To understand behavioral signatures of malware authors through code metrics, bridging cybersecurity and cognitive psychology.
method: Static application security testing and software metrics on leaked malware code compared to benign open-source software.
result: Malware code is smaller, less documented, has higher cyclomatic complexity, and more security issues, but overall quality differences are not extreme.
conclusion: Code metrics can serve as behavioral indicators for cyber offender profiling, but the approach is preliminary and not directly applicable to the user's research areas.

title: AttackPathGNN: Cross-function Vulnerability Detection In Smart Contracts Using State Interference Graphs And Conjunction Pooling
authors: Gabriela Dobrita, Simona-Vasilica Oprea, Adela Bara
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05986v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Existing learning-based detectors for Solidity smart-contracts reduce vulnerability detection to syntactic pattern matching within single functions, yet many of the most consequential exploits (The DAO, Cream Finance) exist not in any individual function but in the relationship between functions and in the combination of conditions that made the attack feasible. Thus, we propose AttackPathGNN, a graph neural network (GNN) that reframes detection as reasoning over explicit attack paths. Two architectural choices distinguish it from prior GNN-based detectors: (1)a State Interference Graph that links every pair of functions sharing mutable storage through typed, weighted edges and through directed reentrancy-path edges defined by an explicit five-condition predicate; (2)conjunction pooling, a differentiable AND-aggregator over eight named exploit preconditions whose log-sigmoid form causes the per-function exploit score to collapse whenever any single mitigation (a reentrancy guard, an access-control modifier or SafeMath) is in place. Across five independent training runs, AttackPathGNN attains 92.3+/-0.2% F1 on the SmartBugs Wild held-out test partition (4.3+/-0.3% false-negative rate, 90.8+/-2.5% detection rate on the independently human-labelled SmartBugs Curated benchmark), recovering 6/10 DASP10 categories at 100% on every seed and Reentrancy at 98.7+/-1.8%. Each prediction is emitted with a structured remediation report, turning each verdict into an actionable, function-level audit finding.
tldr: AttackPathGNN uses graph neural networks to detect cross-function vulnerabilities in smart contracts by modeling state interference and attack paths.
motivation: Existing vulnerability detectors focus on single-function patterns, missing exploits that arise from interactions between functions.
method: The paper proposes a State Interference Graph linking functions via typed edges and a conjunction pooling layer that aggregates exploit preconditions using a differentiable AND operator.
result: The model achieves 92.3% F1 on SmartBugs Wild and recovers 6/10 DASP10 categories at 100% detection on curated benchmarks.
conclusion: AttackPathGNN provides structured remediation reports, enabling actionable audit findings, but its relevance to quantum computing or information thermodynamics is negligible.

title: Double-Directional Wireless Channel Modeling Using Statistics-Aided Machine Learning
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05993v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The double-directional (DD) wireless channel model is important for realistic system design since it provides complete propagation information. While stochastic and deterministic channel models are widely adopted, and existing machine learning (ML) solutions mostly aim to align future channel realizations, these solutions are often limited to short time spans that may not be statistically significant. Moreover, because the number of multi-path components (MPCs) varies with spatial and temporal variation of the receiver (RX) and/or interacting objects (IOs), typical ML solutions that require fixed, predefined input and output shapes fall short. To curb these limitations, we propose a statistics-aided ML solution that relies on a fixed subset of MPCs selection. More specifically, we first select top-[MATH] MPCs, where [MATH] is much smaller than the total number of MPCs, and construct learnable graphs to train our proposed hybrid TimesNet-TimeFilter (TNTF) model. We then use a channel statistics-aided training method to generate future top-M DD channel realizations such that the statistics calculated from these realizations matches closely with those of the actual statistics from the complete time-varying DD channel realizations. We validate the proposed solution using extensive simulations on both synthetic stochastic channel model (SCM)-based and deterministic ray-tracing-based datasets, and demonstrate its effectiveness relative to state-of-the-art baselines.
tldr: This paper proposes a statistics-aided machine learning model for double-directional wireless channel modeling, focusing on multi-path component selection and future channel realization generation.
motivation: Existing stochastic and deterministic channel models and ML solutions are limited by short time spans and inability to handle varying numbers of multi-path components.
method: The authors select top-M multi-path components, construct learnable graphs, and train a hybrid TimesNet-TimeFilter model using channel statistics-aided training to generate future channel realizations.
result: The proposed solution is validated on synthetic stochastic and deterministic ray-tracing datasets, showing effectiveness compared to state-of-the-art baselines.
conclusion: The work provides a novel ML approach for double-directional channel modeling, but its relevance to quantum information science is minimal.

title: Counting Votes With Multisets
authors: Bart Jacobs, Michael Johnson, Richard Buckland
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05218v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A multiset is a 'set' in which elements may occur multiple times. These structures are ideal for expressing the outcome of an election, for instance of the form 60 'yes' and 40 'no'. Moreover, multisets are a useful datatype in vote counting algorithms. This will be illustrated in three different forms of vote counting, known as: 'instant-runoff', 'De Borda', and 'single transferrable vote'. The relevant abstract properties of multisets are: (1) they form a (free) commutative monoid, and (2) they form a functor, and (3) also a monad. This paper illustrates how such categorical properties can be put to good use in deriving and expressing election outcomes. The emphasis is not on the (elementary) category theory involved, but on its application in voting systems.
tldr: This paper uses multisets and category theory to model and analyze three voting systems (instant-runoff, De Borda, single transferable vote), with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To demonstrate the utility of multisets and their categorical properties (commutative monoid, functor, monad) in formalizing vote counting algorithms.
method: The authors apply abstract categorical concepts to derive and express election outcomes for three different voting methods, emphasizing the algebraic structure of multisets.
result: The paper shows how multisets naturally represent vote distributions and how categorical properties simplify reasoning about vote counting algorithms.
conclusion: The work illustrates a novel application of category theory to social choice theory, but has no relevance to the user's research interests in quantum computing, condensed matter physics, or machine learning.

title: The {\alpha} -Discounting ({\alpha}-DMCDM) As An Extension Of Ahp, Topsis, Vikor, Promethee, And Weighted Sum
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05220v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) and other classic Multi-Criteria Decision Making (MCDM) techniques excel when decision makers can provide consistent pair wise judgments. Real world problems, however, often involve inconsistent, n-wise, or non-linear preference structures that render traditional methods inadequate. The {\alpha}-Discounting MCDM ({\alpha}-D MCDM) extends AHP by embedding a global discounting parameter {\alpha} that transforms an inconsistent system of preference equations into a solvable algebraic system.
tldr: This paper extends classic MCDM methods with a discounting parameter to handle inconsistent preferences, but is unrelated to quantum computing, condensed matter physics, or machine learning.
motivation: Classic MCDM methods fail with inconsistent or non-linear preferences; the authors propose a generalization to handle such cases.
method: Introduces a global discounting parameter α that transforms inconsistent preference equations into a solvable algebraic system, extending AHP, TOPSIS, VIKOR, PROMETHEE, and weighted sum.
result: The α-Discounting MCDM method can handle n-wise and non-linear preferences, making it more flexible than traditional approaches.
conclusion: The method broadens the applicability of MCDM to real-world problems with inconsistent data, but no connection to quantum or thermodynamic systems is made.

title: N-ary Quasi-arithmetic Means And Families Without Regularity
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05221v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The classical theorems of Kolmogorov--Nagumo--de Finetti and of Aczel--Maksa characterize quasi-arithmetic means from two complementary directions: the former for compatible families of means satisfying the replacement axiom, and the latter for bisymmetric means of fixed arity. We refine both representation results by showing that the required continuity follows automatically. Our main result states that every reflexive, symmetric, bisymmetric and partially strictly increasing [MATH]-variable operation on a real interval is continuous and hence quasi-arithmetic. The proof is based on a recursive construction on [MATH]-adic rationals given by bisymmetry, and a dense-domain continuity argument. The same method also yields the regularity-free Kolmogorov--Nagumo--de Finetti theorem for compatible families of strictly increasing symmetric means.
tldr: The paper proves that continuity follows from algebraic axioms for quasi-arithmetic means, removing regularity assumptions.
motivation: To refine classical representation theorems for quasi-arithmetic means by showing that continuity is not an independent assumption but a consequence of other axioms.
method: Uses a recursive construction on n-adic rationals via bisymmetry and a dense-domain continuity argument.
result: Every reflexive, symmetric, bisymmetric, and partially strictly increasing n-variable operation on a real interval is continuous and hence quasi-arithmetic.
conclusion: The results strengthen the foundations of mean theory, with implications for aggregation functions and functional equations.

title: The Ize Conjecture Redux: A Parity Criterion For Global Equivariant Bifurcation Guarantees
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05425v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Ize Conjecture proposed that every absolutely irreducible representation of a compact Lie group admits a maximal isotropy subgroup with an odd-dimensional fixed-point space, which would provide a universal bifurcation guarantee via the equivariant degree. Its disproof by Lauterbach and Matthews necessitates a more targeted criterion. We introduce Ize pairs -- pairs [MATH] for which some maximal isotropy subgroup [MATH] satisfies [MATH] -- and prove that this dimension-parity condition completely captures the algebraic obstruction to a non-trivial equivariant degree change at maximal orbit types. Integrating this criterion with a mod-2 equivariant spectral flow yields local and global bifurcation guarantees without recourse to Burnside ring arithmetic. As an application, we establish unbounded branches of non-stationary periodic solutions in a [MATH]-symmetric coupled oscillator network, where the bifurcation guarantees follow entirely from the crossing parity of the linearization at the boundary of a regular parameter window.
tldr: The paper proves a parity criterion for global equivariant bifurcation in symmetric dynamical systems, with an application to coupled oscillator networks.
motivation: The Ize Conjecture, which would guarantee bifurcations for absolutely irreducible representations, was disproven, so a more targeted criterion is needed.
method: The authors introduce Ize pairs and combine a dimension-parity condition with mod-2 equivariant spectral flow to derive bifurcation guarantees without Burnside ring arithmetic.
result: They prove that the parity condition completely captures the algebraic obstruction to nontrivial equivariant degree change at maximal orbit types, and apply it to establish unbounded branches of periodic solutions in a D4-symmetric oscillator network.
conclusion: The work provides a practical criterion for bifurcation analysis in symmetric systems, with potential applications in coupled oscillator networks and other symmetric dynamical systems.

title: Reverse Inequalities For super-Riesz Transforms On Graphs With A Slow Diffusion
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05475v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the [MATH]-dimensional Vicsek graph, we prove that the Riesz-like inequality [MATH] holds for every [MATH] and every [MATH] while it fails whenever [MATH] and [MATH]. Thus, the validity of the inequality remains open only at the critical exponent [MATH]. This provides the first example of an [MATH]-bounded ``super-Riesz transform'', namely an operator of the form [MATH] with [MATH] strictly larger than the Euclidean threshold [MATH]. To achieve this, we establish a more general result linking the diffusion escape rate and a Poincar\'e inequality on balls to the validity of the reverse Riesz-like inequality [MATH].

motivation: To understand the validity of reverse Riesz inequalities on graphs with slow diffusion, particularly for exponents beyond the Euclidean threshold.
method: The authors link diffusion escape rate and Poincaré inequalities on balls to the validity of reverse Riesz-like inequalities, and analyze the Vicsek graph as a specific example.
result: The reverse inequality holds for all p>2 and all q>0 on the Vicsek graph, fails for p<2 and q>0, and remains open at p=2.
conclusion: This provides the first example of an L^p-bounded super-Riesz transform with p>2, opening questions about critical exponents and extensions to other graphs.

title: Unique Ergodicity Of Branched Covers Of Translation Surfaces
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05492v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] be a finite-area translation surface whose vertical flow is uniquely ergodic. Given a slit joining two nonsingular points of [MATH], one can form a branched cyclic cover by gluing [MATH] copies of [MATH] crosswise along the slit. We study when the vertical flow on the resulting cover is uniquely ergodic. We first prove a geometric criterion for unique ergodicity of the branched cover. We show that if, for a sequence of times along the Teichm\"uller geodesic, one endpoint of the slit is contained in embedded Euclidean disks of uniformly positive radius that avoid the other endpoint, then the branched cover is uniquely ergodic. The proof uses the special symmetry of the cover together with an analysis of forward and backward generic points for the vertical flow. We then show that this criterion applies for Lebesgue-almost every choice of slit endpoint under a natural geometric hypothesis on the Teichm\"uller orbit of [MATH], namely a uniform lower bound for the embedded radius along a subsequence. Finally, we give sufficient conditions for such a lower bound in terms of the cylinder geometry of [MATH], introducing the notion of pipe cylinders and proving that embedded disks of definite size must exist. As a consequence, for the class of uniquely ergodic translation surfaces, almost every slit produces a uniquely ergodic branched [MATH]-cover.
tldr: This paper studies unique ergodicity of vertical flows on branched cyclic covers of translation surfaces, a topic in dynamical systems and Teichmüller theory.
motivation: To understand when the vertical flow on a branched cover of a uniquely ergodic translation surface remains uniquely ergodic, extending known results for unbranched covers.
method: The authors prove a geometric criterion involving embedded Euclidean disks along the Teichmüller geodesic, and show it applies for almost every slit endpoint under a uniform lower bound on embedded radius, using pipe cylinders to guarantee such disks.
result: For a uniquely ergodic translation surface, almost every choice of slit produces a uniquely ergodic branched cyclic cover.
conclusion: The work provides a geometric condition for unique ergodicity of branched covers and highlights the role of cylinder geometry, with implications for the study of translation surfaces and their dynamics.

title: Convergence Rate Of The Halpern Iterations With Possibly Distinct Anchor And Initial Guess
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05630v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: All existing convergence rate estimates of Halpern iterations are established only for the case where the anchor coincides with the initial guess. This paper aims to investigate the convergence rate of general Halpern iterations, where the anchor and the initial guess may not necessarily be the same. We present tight convergence rate estimates for both predetermined and adaptive anchoring parameters. These results generalize existing related work.
tldr: This paper studies the convergence rate of Halpern iterations when the anchor and initial guess are different, providing tight estimates for both predetermined and adaptive parameters.
motivation: Existing convergence rate results for Halpern iterations only cover the case where anchor equals initial guess; this work generalizes to distinct anchor and initial guess.
method: The authors analyze the iterative algorithm with two parameters (anchor and initial guess) and derive convergence rates using fixed-point theory and optimization techniques.
result: Tight convergence rate estimates are obtained for both predetermined and adaptive anchoring parameters, generalizing previous results.
conclusion: The findings extend the theoretical understanding of Halpern iterations, with potential applications in optimization and numerical analysis.

title: A Low-rank Interpolatory Projection Algorithm For Solving Large-scale T-Sylvester Equations
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05640v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper considers large-scale T-Sylvester equations of the form [MATH], which admit a low-rank solution. It is shown that when the unique solution of the T-Sylvester equation is low-rank, the problem naturally reduces to a tangential interpolation problem via oblique projection. The specific interpolation points and tangential directions needed to obtain the low-rank solution are not known a priori, thus requiring an iterative approach. An iterative interpolatory projection algorithm is proposed based on these interpolation conditions, which iteratively refines the interpolation data as the projection matrices expand in the number of columns. Numerical examples demonstrate that the proposed algorithm converges with projection matrices having significantly fewer columns compared to existing Krylov-subspace-based projection methods, confirming the superiority of the proposed algorithm over existing approaches.
tldr: This paper proposes an iterative interpolatory projection algorithm for solving large-scale T-Sylvester equations with low-rank solutions.
motivation: T-Sylvester equations arise in various applications, but existing Krylov-subspace methods require large projection spaces; the goal is to develop a more efficient algorithm.
method: The paper shows that low-rank solutions correspond to a tangential interpolation problem and proposes an iterative algorithm that refines interpolation data as projection matrices expand.
result: Numerical examples demonstrate that the proposed algorithm converges with significantly fewer columns than existing Krylov-subspace methods.
conclusion: The algorithm offers a superior approach for solving large-scale T-Sylvester equations, with potential impact on numerical linear algebra and related fields.

title: Benchmarks In Leipzig
authors: Andrei Balakin, Mikl\'os B\'ona, Marie-Charlotte Brandenburg, Clara Briand, Veronica Calvo Cortes, Shelby Cox, Jesus A. de Loera, Danai Deligeorgaki, Hannah Friedman, Tim Gehrunger, Chiara Giardino, Stephen Griffeth, Baran Hashemi, Elena Hoster, Alexander Ivanov, Nupur Jain, Aryaman Jal, Leonie Kayser, Joris Koefler, Kevin K\"uhn, Mario Kummer, Felix Lotter, Ren\'e Marczinzik, Victor S. abstract: ArXiv:2606.05818v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Between April 1 and May 15, 2026, a group of 49 mathematicians compiled a dataset of research-level mathematics questions with known answers. Most of the work was done during the 3-day workshop *Benchmarks in Leipzig* with 35 participants at the Max Planck Institute for Mathematics in the Sciences in Leipzig, Germany. We present the resulting collection of 100 questions. We evaluated these questions in three stages: a single attempt by five state-of-the-art LLMs, followed by a 20-runs-per-model evaluation with three of these models, and finally a 3-run attempt with two heavy-thinking models. After Stage 1, 41 questions remained completely unsolved; after Stage 2, this count dropped to 16; and we concluded Stage 3 with only 2 unsolved questions. This demonstrates that the mathematical reasoning capabilities of LLMs are becoming impressive.
tldr: A workshop compiled 100 research-level math questions to benchmark LLMs, finding that advanced models solved all but two.
motivation: To assess the mathematical reasoning capabilities of state-of-the-art LLMs using a curated set of research-level problems.
method: 49 mathematicians created 100 questions; LLMs were tested in three stages with increasing attempts and model sophistication.
result: After Stage 1, 41 questions unsolved; after Stage 2, 16; after Stage 3, only 2 remained unsolved.
conclusion: LLMs show impressive mathematical reasoning, but some problems remain challenging.

title: Comparison Of Phase-Plane And Trend-Based Qualitative Analysis Of A Dynamic Two-Dimensional Is--lm Model
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05839v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We compare the classical phase-plane analysis of a dynamic two-dimensional IS--LM model with a sign-based trend approach. Applying both methods to the same specification, we examine which qualitative properties of the system can be established solely from sign relations and how these methods can complement each other. In summary, these two approaches capture complementary perspectives on the qualitative behaviour of the considered model, combining the detailed local classification of equilibrium dynamics provided by phase-plane analysis with the broader admissible qualitative structures captured by trend-based analysis.
tldr: This paper compares phase-plane and trend-based qualitative analysis methods for a dynamic two-dimensional IS-LM model in macroeconomics.
motivation: To understand how different qualitative analysis methods can complement each other in studying economic dynamics.
method: Applied both classical phase-plane analysis and sign-based trend analysis to the same IS-LM model specification and compared their qualitative insights.
result: The two methods capture complementary perspectives: phase-plane provides detailed local equilibrium classification, while trend-based analysis captures broader admissible qualitative structures.
conclusion: Combining both methods yields a more complete qualitative understanding of the model's dynamics.

title: Auxiliary Gradient-Flow Solvers For Generalized Newtonian Models
authors: Stefano Zampini, Daniele Boffi, Gurt Dovletov, Peter Markowich
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05926v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce an auxiliary gradient-flow framework for variational problems with generalized Newtonian structure governed by an N-function. The key idea is to replace the nonlinear constitutive dependence on the gradient, or symmetric gradient, by an auxiliary scalar variable representing its squared magnitude. This shifts the nonlinearity from the state equation to the auxiliary variable, yielding a sequence of uniformly elliptic weighted linear problems. At the continuous level, we construct an auxiliary energy on a metric space adapted to the growth of the underlying N-function. In this topology, we prove lower semicontinuity, geodesic [MATH]-convexity, and exponential convergence of the associated minimizing-movement scheme. At the finite element level, we derive a metric gradient flow through an explicit Riesz map, prove global well-posedness of the resulting semi-discrete ODE, and establish convergence to the finite element solution of the Euler--Lagrange equations of the generalized Newtonian energy. For the [MATH]-Laplacian and [MATH]-Stokes models, this gives a rigorous convergence result for [MATH], [MATH], with asymptotic rate estimates beyond this range. We also propose practical time discretizations, including an operator-splitting scheme that gives the \kac iteration as a special case, and an adaptive pseudo-transient method that can be implemented using scalable linear solvers. Numerical experiments for power-law, Carreau--Yasuda, regularized Bingham, and optimal-design models demonstrate robustness, mesh-independent iteration counts in the tested regimes, and performance that matches or outperforms Newton's method.
tldr: This paper introduces an auxiliary gradient-flow framework for solving generalized Newtonian models, focusing on numerical methods for nonlinear PDEs.
motivation: To develop efficient and robust numerical solvers for generalized Newtonian fluid models and related variational problems.
method: Replaces nonlinear gradient dependence with an auxiliary scalar variable, leading to a sequence of linear elliptic problems; uses metric gradient flows and minimizing movement schemes.
result: Proves exponential convergence of the continuous scheme and convergence of finite element discretizations; numerical experiments show robustness and efficiency comparable to Newton's method.
conclusion: The framework provides a practical alternative to Newton's method for generalized Newtonian models, with potential for further extensions.

title: Antilinar Normal Operators On Hilbert Space
abstract: ArXiv:2606.05943v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An operator [MATH] on a complex Hilbert space [MATH] is called antilinear if [MATH] and [MATH] for [MATH] and [MATH]. We investigate some classes of densely defined antilinear unbounded operators, especially antilinear normal operators. We give various characterizations of antilinear normal operators and study a class of such operators in detail. Our main result is a structure theorem for unbounded antilinear normal operators.

motivation: To characterize and classify unbounded antilinear normal operators, which are less studied than linear operators.
method: Mathematical analysis and operator theory, providing definitions, characterizations, and a structure theorem.
result: Various characterizations of antilinear normal operators and a structure theorem for unbounded antilinear normal operators.
